title: AI-Driven Smart Irrigation System Using Edge-Based Embedded Controllers
abstractText: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. This was done by conducting extensive field tests within the semi-arid agricultural areas to prove the efficacy of the recommended solution. The findings show that there is a considerable gain in the efficiency of resources, with up to 38 percent of reduction of water use and 20 percent of increase in the yield of the crops contrasted to the conventional time-based irrigation schemes. Also, the system averaged a latency of only 34millisecs and consumed power at less than 2.5W which became very handy in deployment in rural areas. TinyML and its compatibility with cheap edge hardware are scalable and sustainable, which creates an efficient path to modernize the irrigation infrastructure in the developing world. This article does not only highlight the revolutionary nature of embedded AI in precision agriculture, but it precondition the further innovative development of the field of data-driven farm management and autonomous farm management. The one suggested is one of the options that could be implemented to achieve environmental sustainability, enhance the productivity of agriculture, and make smart and local decisions to use water intelligently.

title: Internalisasi Nilai Moral dalam Pembelajaran PPKn Sebagai Upaya Pembentukan Karakter Kewarganegaraan Siswa Sekolah Dasar
abstractText: Pendidikan memegang peranan penting dalam pembentukan karakter dan moral peserta didik sebagai bagian dari upaya mewujudkan tujuan nasional. Dalam konteks Indonesia, Pancasila menjadi dasar utama pendidikan karakter yang perlu ditanamkan sejak sekolah dasar, karena pada tahap ini kepribadian anak mulai terbentuk. Artikel ini membahas internalisasi nilai moral, peran Pendidikan Pancasila dan Kewarganegaraan (PPKn) dalam penanaman nilai moral, serta nilai-nilai moral yang relevan bagi peserta didik sekolah dasar. Metode yang digunakan adalah studi literatur melalui penelaahan buku, jurnal ilmiah, dan dokumen pendidikan terkait. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa pembelajaran PPKn berkontribusi signifikan dalam menumbuhkan karakter kewarganegaraan siswa yang jujur, bertanggung jawab, toleran, dan memiliki kepedulian sosial. Proses internalisasi nilai moral akan berjalan optimal apabila dilaksanakan secara terencana dan berkesinambungan melalui keteladanan guru, pembiasaan, serta pembelajaran kontekstual yang sesuai dengan kehidupan siswa. Oleh karena itu, pendidikan moral di sekolah dasar tidak hanya berfokus pada penanaman nilai, tetapi juga berfungsi sebagai strategi utama dalam menyiapkan generasi yang berkarakter, berintegritas, dan mampu berperan positif dalam kehidupan bermasyarakat.

title: FROM INFLUENCE TO INTENT: SYSTEMATICALLY REVIEWING THE ROLE OF SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCERS IN PURCHASING BEHAVIOUR
abstractText: Background: In the digital moving age, social media influencers (SMIs) have emerged as strong agents altering consumer behaviour and hence, there was a need to conduct systematic literature analysis present on social media influencers.Objectives: Broadly, to explore the impact of social media influencers on consumer purchase behaviour.Methods: This systematic literature review explores the impact of social media influencers on consumer purchase behaviour, synthesizing findings from academic research published over the period of 15 years (2011 to 2025). PRISMA is being used as the methodology for conducting this literature review.Results: The review identifies key factors such as influencer credibility, authenticity, engagement, content quality, and platform characteristics that prominently influence consumer trust and By employing, simultaneously, their buying behaviour.Conclusion: Social media influencers significantly impact consumer trust and buying behaviour. The review categorizes the literature into thematic clusters, including influencer marketing strategies and consumer psychology.

title: Cyber Soldier project - A threat-led methodology for assessing the Digital Resilience of cybersecurity systems
abstractText: In order to comply with European regulatory frameworks like the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), we propose the Cyber Soldier approach and tool set, which presents a threat-led approach for evaluating the digital resilience of cybersecurity systems inside enterprises. This approach, in contrast to conventional vulnerability assessments or penetration testing, focuses on simulating the tactics, methods, and procedures (TTPs) of actual attackers in order to assess the efficacy of operational resilience mechanisms and cybersecurity measures in production systems. In order to assess the organization's readiness for complex cyberthreats, the suggested approach combines threat information, red team scenario creation, and detection performance analysis into a single procedure. We show how the proposed framework connects the operational practice of resilience testing with the strategic compliance obligations under DORA. We also provide some preliminary statistics about the use of the Cyber Soldier toolkit in practical settings.

title: DETECTION OF BITCOIN FRAUD USING VARIATIONAL AUTO ENCODER AND LIGHT GRADIENT BOOSTING MACHINE
abstractText: The proliferation of fraudulent behaviour in cryptocurrency ecosystems poses a significant threat to financial security infrastructure. This study develops an approach that uses Variational Autoencoders in combination with Light Gradient Boosting Machines for detecting fraudulent Bitcoin transactions. The Variational Autoencoder component encodes each transaction into a compact latent representation, which is concatenated with the original transaction features to enrich the representation available to the classifier. The Light Gradient Boosting Machine is responsible for classification. Experimental validation on the Elliptic dataset of bitcoin transactions shows the model achieves 99.2% accuracy and 96% F1 score for minority-class detection, outperforming other methods such as Random Forest (95.9% F1), ANN-based models (89.8% F1), and ensemble stacking (97% F1). These results far exceed those of previous approaches, demonstrating the model’s ability to enhance the security and integrity of cryptocurrency transactions.

title: A LIGHTWEIGHT CUSTOM CNN FOR ROBUST AND CLINICALLY SAFE CT KIDNEY DISEASE CLASSIFICATION
abstractText: ABSTRACT: Kidney diseases such as renal cysts, stone, and malignant tumors represent a significant and increasing health burden worldwide. Manual CT diagnosis is labour-intensive and has high inter-observer variability, which requires the support of automatic diagnosis. In this paper, a lightweighted custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is proposed, which is used to automatically classify kidney computed tomography (CT) images into four classes: Cyst, Normal, Stone, and Tumor. It includes residual skip connections, a dual-pooling head (Global Average and Global Max Pooling), Spatial Dropout2D regularization, and a composite training objective that explicitly favors Tumor Recall. The CT-KIDNEY-DATASET was mad leakage-safe through MD5 exact deduplication and perceptual-hash grouping, so that all reported evaluations are free of data leakage. Across the five validation folds, KidneyCNN achieved a mean accuracy of 99.82 ± 0.06% and a mean Tumor Recall of 99.31 ± 0.30%. Separately, ensemble inference on the independent held-out test set of 1,904 images achieved 99.84% accuracy, with AUC = 1.000 for all classes and only three misclassifications. The Grad-CAM++ results show that the model attention as anatomically relevant, which further indicates that KidneyCNN is a clinically safe and deployable kidney disease screening tool.

title: Factores Socioeconómicos Asociados a la Permanencia Universitaria: Un Análisis desde las Políticas de Bienestar Estudiantil
abstractText: Justification: Student persistence remains a major challenge for public higher education in Ecuador. For many students, gaining access to university does not necessarily mean completing their studies, particularly when economic hardship threatens academic continuity. Objectives: To examine the relationship between perceptions of institutional financial aid, knowledge of the regulations governing it, socioeconomic conditions, and perceived student persistence. Methodology: A quantitative secondary data analysis with a non-experimental, cross-sectional, and correlational design was conducted. The sample consisted of 139 students receiving financial aid at an Ecuadorian public university. The data came from a previously validated 48-item questionnaire and were analyzed using Spearman correlations, Mann-Whitney U tests, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and multiple linear regression. Results: More favorable perceptions of financial aid were significantly associated with higher perceived student persistence (rs = 0.59; p < 0.001). A model including perceptions of financial aid and knowledge of institutional regulations explained 39.8% of the variance, whereas socioeconomic conditions did not reach statistical significance. Aid covered academic and institutional expenses better than subsistence-related needs, and 86.8% agreed that financial reasons influenced thoughts of withdrawal. Conclusions: These findings highlight the importance of understanding financial aid not only as economic support but also as a key strategy for promoting student persistence within higher education welfare policies.

title: Transformational Leadership, Organizational Culture, Career Development, and Work Motivation as Determinants of Lecturer Performance in Private Universities
abstractText: This study examined the effects of transformational leadership, organizational culture, and career development on lecturer performance and tested work motivation as a mediating mechanism. A quantitative ex post facto survey design was applied to 227 lecturers drawn proportionally from a population of 526 lecturers at three private universities in Bireuen Regency, Aceh. Data were collected using five-point Likert questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with reflective–reflective higher-order constructs. The results show that transformational leadership significantly predicted work motivation (β = 0.349, t = 6.306, p < 0.001), followed by organizational culture (β = 0.251, t = 4.082, p < 0.001) and career development (β = 0.239, t = 4.123, p < 0.001). All three organizational factors also had significant direct effects on lecturer performance, while work motivation was the strongest direct predictor (β = 0.318, t = 4.838, p < 0.001). Work motivation partially mediated the effects of transformational leadership (β = 0.111), organizational culture (β = 0.080), and career development (β = 0.076). The model explained 42.9% of the variance in work motivation and 50.7% of the variance in lecturer performance. The findings imply that sustainable lecturer performance requires an integrated strategy combining inspirational leadership, supportive organizational culture, structured career development, and deliberate strengthening of work motivation.

title: SECOND LIFE ASSESSMENT OF SALVAGED 18650 LITHIUM-ION CELLS USING CAPACITY AND INTERNAL RESISTANCE METRICS
abstractText: The increasing waste stream of end-of-first-life lithium-ion batteries poses an important challenge and a circular economy opportunity via second-life applications. Nonetheless, trusted characterisation strategies are critical for confirming the safety and functionality of repurposed cells. This study analyses the viability of 18650 cells salvaged from laptop, power tool, and electric vehicle (EV) battery packs according to a dual-parameter framework based on residual capacity (State of Health, SoH) and DC internal resistance (DCIR). Measured SoH ranged from 50.0% to 98.0%, and DCIR ranged from 90 to 500 mΩ across the 22 characterised cells. This is, to our knowledge, among the first studies to combine dual-parameter screening with an explicit threshold sensitivity analysis across three distinct salvaged cell chemistries. Although 77.3% of the 22 characterised cells continued to possess a SoH ≥ 70%, only one cell (4.5%) passed a conservative reuse threshold in which both SoH ≥ 70% and the direct current internal resistance (DCIR) were < 100 mΩ. SoH showed a strong inverse correlation with DCIR (Pearson r = −0.76, R² = 0.57). Cells from the EV system showed maximum SoH retention with fair DCIR readings. The findings show that internal resistance, rather than capacity fade alone, is a key limiting factor to second-life applicability for power-demanding uses and highlight the need for multi-parameter screening protocols including resistance to reduce risks of unwanted low-performing battery reuse.

title: Quarter Life Crisis dalam Perspektif Al-Qur'an: Kajian Tafsir Tematik terhadap Konsep Arah Hidup dan Kematangan Spiritual
abstractText: Fenomena Quarter Life Crisis (QLC) menjadi salah satu persoalan yang banyak dialami generasi muda pada rentang usia 20–30 tahun. Krisis ini ditandai oleh kebingungan menentukan arah hidup, kecemasan terhadap masa depan, serta pencarian identitas diri yang sering kali memengaruhi kondisi psikologis dan spiritual. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis konsep arah hidup dan kematangan spiritual dalam menghadapi Quarter Life Crisis berdasarkan perspektif Al-Qur'an. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode tafsir tematik (maudhu‘i) yang mengacu pada langkah-langkah penafsiran al-Farmawi. Data penelitian berupa ayat-ayat Al-Qur'an yang berkaitan dengan tujuan penciptaan manusia, pemanfaatan waktu, keteladanan pemuda, serta nilai-nilai keimanan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Al-Qur'an menawarkan kerangka konseptual untuk mengatasi QLC melalui peneguhan orientasi hidup berbasis ibadah, penguatan iman, amal saleh, kesabaran, syukur, dan tawakal. Kisah Ashabul Kahfi dan Nabi Yusuf juga menunjukkan bahwa fase krisis dapat menjadi sarana pembentukan karakter dan kematangan spiritual. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa Quarter Life Crisis dalam perspektif Al-Qur'an tidak dipandang sebagai fase yang melemahkan, melainkan sebagai momentum untuk melakukan reorientasi hidup, memperkuat syakhsiyah Islamiyah, dan mencapai kematangan spiritual sesuai tujuan penciptaan manusia.

title: PERAN MEDIASI STRES AKADEMIK DALAM HUBUNGAN DUKUNGAN SOSIAL DAN TEKANAN AKADEMIK TERHADAP KINERJA AKADEMIK MAHASISWA
abstractText: Studi ini menganalisis pengaruh dukungan sosial dan tekanan akademik terhadap prestasi akademik mahasiswa, dengan stres akademik sebagai variabel mediasi. Penelitian ini dilakukan karena studi-studi sebelumnya sebagian besar meneliti hubungan langsung antar variabel-variabel tersebut secara terpisah, sementara studi yang mengintegrasikannya melalui mediasi stres akademik masih terbatas. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei digunakan. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner yang dibagikan kepada 83 mahasiswa aktif dari beberapa institusi pendidikan tinggi dan dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares (PLS) dengan perangkat lunak SmartPLS. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa dukungan sosial berpengaruh positif terhadap prestasi akademik dan stres akademik. Tekanan akademik memiliki pengaruh positif yang kuat terhadap stres akademik dan pengaruh negatif terhadap prestasi akademik. Stres akademik juga memengaruhi prestasi akademik dan memediasi hubungan antara dukungan sosial, tekanan akademik, dan prestasi akademik. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa manajemen stres akademik yang efektif dan dukungan sosial yang lebih kuat sangat penting untuk meningkatkan prestasi akademik mahasiswa dan menjaga kesejahteraan psikologis mereka di lingkungan pendidikan tinggi.

title: Pengaruh Kepuasan Kerja dan Keterikatan Karyawan terhadap Niatan Berpindah pada PT Global Yimi Cargo Cabang Tangerang
abstractText: Employees who plan to leave are costly for courier and cargo firms, since every resignation triggers new hiring and interrupts day-to-day operations. This article investigates how far job satisfaction and employee engagement shape the turnover intention of back office staff at PT Global Yimi Cargo, Tangerang Branch. The design is an explanatory quantitative survey. All 96 back office staff took part (saturated sampling) and completed a 30-item questionnaire on a five-point Likert scale. Once the instrument proved valid and reliable and the classical assumptions were met, the responses were processed with multiple linear regression in SPSS. Job satisfaction was found to lower turnover intention (t = -4.062; p = 0.000). Employee engagement, in contrast, showed no meaningful effect when tested on its own (t = 1.668; p = 0.099). Tested jointly, the two predictors remained meaningful (F = 9.062; p = 0.000), although the model accounted for only 14.5% of the variation in turnover intention. This pattern suggests that feeling satisfied with the job, rather than feeling energized by it, is what mostly keeps staff from leaving. Pay and promotion opportunities received the lowest ratings, so fixing compensation and career paths deserves first place in the retention program of the company.

title: Preoperative Factors Associated With Pulmonary Embolism Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty: An ACS-NSQIP Analysis of 2017–2021 Data
abstractText: Background This study examined preoperative factors associated with 30-day pulmonary embolism (PE) after primary total hip arthroplasty. Methods ACS-NSQIP records from 2017–2021 with CPT code 27130 were analyzed. Complete cases were included using cleaned body mass index (BMI), age, sex, steroid use, and disseminated cancer. These five variables were entered jointly into logistic regression. Results Among 196,495 complete cases, 484 (0.246%) had PE. Adjusted odds ratios were 6.44 for disseminated cancer, 1.69 for steroid use, 1.23 for female sex, 1.041 per year of age, and 1.031 per kg/m² of BMI (all P < .05). Apparent AUC was 0.647 (95% CI, 0.622–0.672). The Hosmer–Lemeshow test indicated lack of fit (P = .012). Conclusions Five preoperative characteristics were associated with PE. Discrimination was modest, calibration limitations were present, and validation is required before clinical use.

title: Pengaruh Price Earning Ratio dan Dividend Yield terhadap Return Saham Perusahaan Subsektor Makanan dan Minuman di BEI 2020-2024
abstractText: This study analyzes the effect of Price Earning Ratio (PER) and Dividend Yield (DY) on Stock Return in food and beverage subsector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020-2024 period. A quantitative descriptive method was applied to secondary data obtained from the annual financial statements and stock prices of the sample companies. Using a purposive sampling technique, eight companies were selected, producing 40 firm year observations. Data wew analyzed through classical assumption tests (normlaity, multicollinearuty, heterocedasticity, and autocorrelation), multiple linear regression, partial t tests, a simultaneous F test, and the coefficient of determination (R2), processed with SPSS version 27. The partial test results show that PER has a negative and insignificant effect on Stock Return (coefficient -0.104; t = -0,471 ; sig. = 0.641), and DY also has a negative and insignificant effect (coefficient – 1,907; t= - 0,629 ; sig. = 0,533). The simultaneous tes indicates that PER and DY together have no significant effect on stock return(F) = 0,225; sig. = 0,800). With an R2 of only 0.012, meaning the two variables explain merely 1.2% of stock return variation. These findings imply that investors and companies in this subsector should not rely solely on PER and DY when assessing stock performance, but should also consider other fundamental and macroeconomic indicators.

Optimal Reticulocyte Hemoglobin Equivalent Cutoff to Diagnose Iron Deficiency: A Study from South Indian Population
abstractText: Abstract Background: Anemia is the most common health problem affecting approximately one-third of the population worldwide, with 50% of patients suffering from iron-deficiency anemia (IDA). Hematological parameters along with peripheral smear finding may help in picking up patients with IDA but are insensitive to early stages of iron deficiency. Serum iron studies are required for confirmation but these are affected by inflammation, infection, and liver disease. Reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent (Ret He) measures the hemoglobin (HGB) content in circulating reticulocytes, reflecting iron availability for erythropoiesis over the preceding 3–4 days and it is not influenced by inflammation or diurnal variation and provides a real-time assessment of iron deficiency. However, Ret He cutoff show variation across different population. Methods: This cross-sectional study done at a tertiary care health center in South India, for the period of 2 years (September 2024–February 2026). The study population includes individuals more than 18 years of age and is categorized into two categories. Category I composed of 100 normal individuals with HGB values and serum iron studies within normal limits. Category II comprising of 200 individuals having serum ferritin levels <30 ng/mL or transferrin saturation (T-SAT) of <20%. Results: Comparison of the mean values of parameters such as HGB, red blood cell (RBC) count, RBC indices, reticulocyte parameters, Ret He, serum iron, T-SAT, and serum ferritin levels were reduced below normal limits in cases with iron deficiency. A strong statistically significant positive correlation is observed with mean corpuscular hemoglobin (r = 0.823), mean corpuscular volume (r = 0.8186), and HGB (r = 0.8165). Moderate positive correlations are evident with key iron profile parameters, including T-SAT%, serum iron, and ferritin. Receiver operating characteristic analysis Ret He cutoff of 29.85 pg was obtained which showed 85% sensitivity and 88% specificity with excellent area under the curve of 0.941 and statistically significant P < 0.001 in predicting iron deficiency. Conclusion: Reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent (Ret-He) is a reliable and effective marker for detecting iron deficiency, demonstrating excellent diagnostic accuracy, with a cutoff of 29.85 pg. Its incorporation into routine hematological evaluation may facilitate early identification of iron deficiency, although population-specific cutoffs should be considered.

title: STEAM and Computational Thinking in Technology-Enhanced Education: A Systematic Review of Learning Design
abstractText: This systematic literature review examines how STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics) and computational thinking (CT) activities are conceptualized and implemented in technology-enhanced learning environments in primary and lower secondary education. Guided by PRISMA 2020 procedures, 34 empirical studies were analyzed using inductive content analysis to identify recurring pedagogical structures. Seven categories emerged: problem-based, inquiry-based, and project-based pedagogical forms; a social dimension of collaborative learning; and modal formats including role-playing, game-based, and experiential learning. These categories reflect patterns of pedagogical organization rather than disciplinary content alone. Interpreted through the lens of active learning, the findings indicate that STEAM and CT activities are predominantly structured as activity-centered, interdisciplinary, and iterative learning processes. CT appears not as an isolated technological skill but as a structuring principle for organizing reasoning, problem decomposition, and solution refinement across subject domains. Overall, the reviewed studies suggest that STEAM–CT integration increasingly functions as a model of learning design and orchestration: CT organizes sequences of cognitive actions, while active learning formats cultivate epistemic practices (investigating, designing, testing, and refining) realized through the interaction of tools, artifacts, and collaborative structures. This positioning highlights STEAM and CT as integral to contemporary science, mathematics, and technology education.

title: Validation of 3D intraoral scanner use for detecting caries lesions around dental restorations: A diagnostic accuracy study
abstractText: Abstract Objectives This study aimed to validate the use of a 3D intraoral scanner (IOS) for detecting secondary caries lesions around restorations using image-based CARS-derived severity categories, compared with visual-tactile clinical examination. Materials and methods A diagnostic validation study was conducted at the university clinical facilities, from July 2023 to September 2024, including adult patients with amalgam or composite resin restorations on anterior and posterior teeth. The restorations were assessed using visual-tactile clinical examination, adopted as the clinical reference standard, and IOS image-based assessment. Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, binary-classification AUC, and clinical–IOS agreement were estimated. Confidence intervals for diagnostic accuracy measures were obtained using participant-level cluster bootstrap resampling. Results A total of 299 restorations in 41 patients were assessed. IOS sensitivity varied, with 75% (95% CI: 66.2–82.0) at the initial lesion threshold, 40% (95% CI: 20.8–57.7) at the moderate lesion threshold, and 57.1% (95% CI: 33.3–100.0) at the severe lesion threshold. Specificity was consistently high, with 84.1% (95% CI: 78.7–89.4), 97.4% (95% CI: 95.6–99.2), and 99.7% (95% CI: 98.7–99.7) at the initial, moderate, and severe lesion thresholds, respectively. Binary-classification AUC values were 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75–0.84), 0.69 (95% CI: 0.58–0.78), and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.66–1.00) at the initial, moderate, and severe lesion thresholds, respectively. Positive predictive value was highest at the severe lesion threshold (80%), while the negative predictive value was especially high at this threshold (99%). Exact clinical-IOS agreement was 77.9%, whereas linearly weighted observed agreement was 91.1%, with a linearly weighted kappa coefficient of 0.53. Conclusions The 3D intraoral scanner is a complementary tool for assessing secondary caries lesions, showing high specificity across lesion thresholds. Sensitivity varied according to lesion severity and was less precise at the severe threshold due to the small number of severe lesions. Future research should increase sample sizes and explore combining IOS with other diagnostic methods to improve detection, especially for moderate lesions and higher caries prevalence. Clinical Relevance Conventional IOS images may assist in documenting and assessing visible changes around restorations. Clinical interpretation should consider the observed sensitivity limitations and incorporate visual-tactile examination and radiographic assessment when indicated.

title: Age-related Upper Airway Changes and Their Significance in Orthodontic Treatment Planning: A Scoping Review
abstractText: Abstract Orthodontic treatment outcomes and airway stability may be impacted by age-related changes in upper airway morphology and function, especially in adults. A thorough search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. PRISMA-ScR guidelines were used to analyze and select the studies that were associated with aging, craniofacial morphology, and orthodontic or orthognathic interventions. Aging is related to reduction in airway volume, decreased neuromuscular tone, soft-tissue laxity, and increased airway collapsibility are associated with aging. Vertical skeletal pattern variations and craniofacial aging may further compromise the airway dimensions. Airway dimensions are also affected by the orthodontic treatment modality. Minimal clinically significant airway compromise is seen in extraction therapy, whereas favorable airway outcomes are seen in mandibular advancement and orthognathic surgery. Age-related airway changes are important considerations in orthodontic treatment planning. Individualized airway assessment and interdisciplinary management are essential to optimize functional and respiratory outcomes.

Pengaruh Budaya Kerja dan Disiplin Kerja Terhadap Kinerja Karyawan Jasamarga Metropolitan Tollroad Regional Division
abstractText: Jasamarga Metropolitan Tollroad Regional Division is a company that specializes in toll road management and toll road services. The focus of this study is to identify the influence of work culture and work discipline on the performance of employees at Jasamarga Metropolitan Tollroad Regional Division. The method used is a quantitative associative-causal analysis. The research sample consisted of 60 people using a saturated sample. Questionnaires were distributed to collect data both online and offline, and the data were analyzed using IBM SPSS. The results of the partial tests indicated that work culture has a positive and significant effect on employee performance, and that work discipline has a positive and significant effect on employee performance. The multiple regression test revealed that work culture and work discipline have a positive and significant effect on employee performance. The percentage of employee performance attributed to work culture and work discipline is 52%, while 48% is attributed to other aspects. This research indicates that work culture and work discipline are factors that influence the performance of employees at the Jasamarga Metropolitan Tollroad Regional Division.

abstractText: La investigación tiene como objetivo determinar la relación de las buenas prácticas de gestión empresarial y transparencia de los estados financieros de las pequeñas empresas de la provincia de Trujillo, 2024-2025. El estudio por su naturaleza fue aplicado, con enfoque cuantitativo, alcance descriptivo-correlacional, diseño no experimental, transversal. La técnica utilizada fue la encuesta y el análisis de fuentes bibliográficas. La muestra corresponde a 85 empresas de una población de 710. Como resultados, se determinó una correlación Rho de Spearman de 0,842 en el año 2024 y en el año 2025 de 0,741 entre buenas prácticas de gestión empresarial y transparencia de estados financieros, con un nivel de significancia (bilateral) de 0,000, siendo que, al ser menor a 0,05. Como conclusión general, se determinó que las buenas prácticas de gestión empresarial se relacionan de manera positiva y fuerte con la transparencia de estados financieros en la provincia de Trujillo, 2024-2025. Asimismo, al optimizarse las buenas prácticas de gestión empresarial, se optimiza la transparencia de estados financieros en 47.1% (año 2024) y en 28.2% (año 2025), lo que significa que la optimización de las actividades de buenas prácticas mejora la transparencia de estados financieros de las empresas.

How Artificial Intelligence Is Reshaping the Work and Career Paths of Junior Software Developers in China and the United States
abstractText: The widespread adoption of generative AI in software development can impact junior developers as AI tools can help with coding, testing, debugging, and documentation tasks. This paper will explore how AI influences the job, the necessary skills, and the career paths of junior software engineers, and why this can vary across different countries, such as China and the USA. Experiments, job-vacancy studies, surveys, government statistics, and industry evidence are the bases for the analysis. While results have been inconsistent for different tasks and contexts, research indicates that AI can boost developer productivity, with one field experiment finding it has a greater impact on less-experienced developers. There is more code being written, more code to be reviewed, and more code to be communicated and understood because of AI's increasing automation of repetitive tasks and coding. While software developers should still be in demand, competition for jobs in this field might increase. The direct evidence of changes in junior hiring is more pronounced in the United States, while China has a massive developer community and a growing domestic AI industry. In conclusion, the evidence points to the evolution of the junior developer position, not its demise, due to the influence of AI.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Risk Factors for Major Complications in Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis: A Single-Institution Retrospective Study
abstractText: Background and Objectives Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) is a rare HPVassociated disease characterized by recurrent papillomatous lesions within the airway.Subjects and Method We retrospectively analyzed 165 patients who were treated for RRP at a single tertiary institution between 2005 and 2021 and evaluated clinical characteristics, treatment outcomes, and risk factors for major complications.Results Juvenile-onset RRP (JO-RRP) accounted for 11.5% of the cases, demonstrating a significantly more aggressive clinical course than adult-onset RRP (AO-RRP). JO-RRP patients showed markedly higher rates of subglottic spread, tracheotomy, and laryngeal stenosis, while no cases achieved remission. CO2, PDL, and KTP lasers were used for surgical treatment, often combined with intralesional cidofovir injection and HPV vaccination. Our findings suggest that JO-RRP is associated with poor prognosis and aggressive airway involvement. Tracheotomy and repeated surgeries are highly likely to serve as indicators reflecting disease severity, a prolonged disease course, lower respiratory tract involvement, and airway obstruction.Conclusion These findings suggest that continuous surveillance for complications is essential in patients with a high disease burden.

title: Pengaruh Beban Kerja dan Stres Kerja terhadap Turnover Intention Karyawan Chong Qing Hot Pot PIM 3 Jakarta Selatan
abstractText: High employee turnover is one of the issues that can affect a company’s operational effectiveness. Turnover intention refers to an employee’s desire to leave the company due to various factors, including workload and job stress. This study aims to analyze the effect of workload and job stress on employees’ turnover intention at Chong Qing Hot Pot PIM 3 Branch. This study employs a quantitative research method, using a questionnaire distributed to 30 employees of Chong Qing Hot Pot PIM 3 Branch. Using Statistical Product and Service Solutions (SPSS) version 26, the data analysis techniques included validity testing, reliability testing, classical assumption testing, multiple linear regression analysis, the coefficient of determination (R²) test, the partial test (t-test), and the simultaneous test (F-test). The findings indicate that workload has no significant effect on turnover intention, with a significance level of 0.598 (>0.05), while job stress has a positive and significant effect on turnover intention, with a significance level of 0.032 (<0.05). Simultaneously, workload and job stress have a significant effect on turnover intention, with a significance level of 0.000 (<0.05). The Adjusted R Square value of 0.452 indicates that workload and job stress explain 45.2% of the variation in turnover intention, while the remaining 54.8% is explained by other factors not examined in this study.

title: Capacity and Disposition: A Framework for Understanding GenAI Engagement in Assessment Practice
abstractText: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has made assessment work faster, messier, and more consequential. This conceptual article argues that assessment professionals’ engagement with GenAI is shaped less by simple enthusiasm or resistance than by the relationship between two conditions: the time professionals have to learn, test, and implement AI responsibly, and the disposition they bring to AI-mediated assessment practice. Institutional support functions as the environment that expands or constrains both. The article proposes the Capacity-Disposition Framework, a model that identifies four engagement conditions: The Calendar Trap, The Margin Lab, The Evidence Gate, and The Practice Commons. The framework helps assessment leaders diagnose uneven AI adoption, protect time for meaningful experimentation, honor appropriate skepticism, and connect AI use to validity, equity, transparency, and continuous improvement rather than speed alone.

ASSOCIATION OF FOKI AND BSMI RFLP GENOTYPES IN VDR GENE WITH HASHIMOTO’S THYROIDITIS IN ERBIL PROVINCE
abstractText: Genetic variations in the Vitamin-D-receptor (VDR) gene have been associated with the pathogenesis of several immune-mediated conditions, notably Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (HT). This work was undertaken to assess whether the widely studied FokI (rs2228570) and BsmI (rs1544410) two well-characterized VDR polymorphisms are associated with susceptibility to HT among females in Erbil Province in the Iraqi Kurdish region. The design of this study was case-control, with 50 female patients diagnosed with HT and 50 healthy female controls, both age-matched (24-59 years). With the guidance of a qualified endocrinologist, various biochemical indicators have been methodically evaluated such as TSH, FT4 and anti-thyroid peroxidase (A-TPO) and Vitamin D3. Genotyping of both polymorphic loci was accomplished via the PCR-restriction fragment length polymorphism (PCR-RFLP) approach. Neither genotype nor allele distributions were differed significantly between groups for either polymorphism (P>0.05). This result was also confirmed by Fisher's exact test, which revealed no significant relationship in genotypic and allelic distribution (P > 0.05). Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium was maintained for the FokI locus in both groups (P > 0.05). For the BsmI polymorphism, however, no similar difference was found, as HWE was only seen in patients, but not in controls (P> 0.05 vs P <0.05). Taken together, the data provide no evidence linking FokI or BsmI variants to Hashimoto’s thyroiditis susceptibility in this female Erbil Province population, and VDR variant frequencies were not different meaningfully between cases and control.

title: Effects of loading angle and build direction on the tensile behavior of WAAM steel produced with ER70S-6 welding wire
abstractText: This study investigates the effects of loading angle and build direction on the tensile properties of components fabricated through wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) fabricated using ER70S-6 steel. Tensile tests were conducted at four loading angles (0°, 45°, 60°, and 90°) for two build directions (flat and upright). For each loading angle and build direction, two tensile specimens were tested, and the reported values were obtained from a representative specimen for each testing condition. The results reveal that the WAAM-fabricated specimens exhibited pronounced mechanical anisotropy, with the highest tensile strength obtained when the applied load is parallel to the bead direction, followed by a considerable reduction at other loading angles. For the upright build direction, the ultimate tensile strength decreased by approximately 47% at 450 relative to that at 0°, suggesting a possible contribution from interlayer shear stresses and delamination-related failure mechanisms. An empirical model was proposed to describe the dependence of tensile strength on the loading angle, enabling the quantitative evaluation of the role of different stress components. The flat build direction exhibited more stable mechanical behavior and a lower degree of anisotropy. In addition, hardness measurements showed that the variation in hardness was mainly governed by the build direction rather than the loading angle. The obtained results provide further insight into the relationship among layered structure, stress state, and mechanical properties, thereby supporting the design and application of WAAM structures subjected to multidirectional loading conditions.

title: Sentido de la vida y espiritualidad en pacientes con tratamiento de hemodiálisis: revisión integrativa
abstractText: La enfermedad renal crónica constituye un problema de salud pública que afecta la calidad de vida de los pacientes, especialmente aquellos sometidos a hemodiálisis, quienes experimentan repercusiones físicas, emocionales y espirituales. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar la evidencia científica reciente sobre el sentido de la vida y la espiritualidad en pacientes en hemodiálisis. Se realizó una revisión narrativa de literatura en las bases de datos PubMed, Scopus y SciELO, considerando artículos originales publicados entre 2017 y 2025 en inglés y español. Se seleccionaron dieciocho estudios que cumplían con los criterios de inclusión y se organizaron en una matriz de análisis. Los resultados evidencian que la espiritualidad y el sentido de la vida se relacionan de manera positiva con la esperanza, la resiliencia, la adherencia al tratamiento y la autoestima, mientras que las intervenciones espirituales reportan mejoras en el bienestar psicológico y en la calidad de vida. Se concluye que la espiritualidad y el sentido de la vida son dimensiones esenciales en pacientes hemodializados, cuya integración en el cuidado de enfermería permite un abordaje integral, humanizado y orientado al bienestar.

title: SELF-IDENTIFICATION MEMEDIASI HUBUNGAN ANTARA PERSEPSI MANFAAT KONTEN SELF DIAGNOSIS DAN KECEMASAN REMAJA
abstractText: ABSTRACT Adolescents increasingly use social media to obtain mental health information, including through self-diagnosis content. However, the mechanisms linking perceived benefits of such content to anxiety symptoms remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine self-identification as a statistical mediator in the association between perceived benefits of self-diagnosis content on social media and anxiety symptoms among adolescents. A quantitative approach was employed, involving 213 senior high school students in Indonesia recruited through purposive sampling. Data were collected using measures of perceived content benefits, self-identification, and anxiety symptoms, and analyzed using Spearman’s rank correlations and a simple mediation model with unstandardized coefficients. The results indicated that perceived benefits were positively correlated with self-identification (ρ = 0.671, p < 0.001) and anxiety symptoms (ρ = 0.672, p < 0.001). Self-identification was also positively correlated with anxiety symptoms (ρ = 0.703, p < 0.001). Mediation analysis revealed a significant indirect effect of perceived benefits on anxiety symptoms through self-identification (b = 1.709, SE = 0.1055, 95% CI [1.503, 1.916]), while the direct effect remained significant (b = 0.473, SE = 0.0922, 95% CI [0.292, 0.654]). These findings support partial statistical mediation. The results suggest that identifying with mental health narratives on social media is associated with anxiety symptoms among adolescents. Therefore, digital mental health literacy programs in schools should incorporate critical evaluation of online content and awareness of the potential risks of self-labeling. ABSTRAK Media sosial semakin banyak digunakan remaja untuk memperoleh informasi mengenai kesehatan mental, termasuk melalui konten self-diagnosis. Namun, mekanisme yang menghubungkan persepsi manfaat konten tersebut dengan gejala kecemasan masih perlu dikaji. Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji peran self-identification sebagai mediator statistik dalam hubungan antara persepsi manfaat konten self-diagnosis di media sosial dan gejala kecemasan pada remaja. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan melibatkan 213 siswa sekolah menengah atas di Indonesia yang direkrut melalui teknik purposif. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan instrumen persepsi manfaat konten, self-identification, dan gejala kecemasan, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan korelasi Spearman dan analisis mediasi sederhana dengan koefisien tidak terstandarisasi. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa persepsi manfaat berkorelasi positif dengan self-identification (ρ = 0,671; p < 0,001) dan gejala kecemasan (ρ = 0,672; p < 0,001). Self-identification juga berkorelasi positif dengan gejala kecemasan (ρ = 0,703; p < 0,001). Analisis mediasi menunjukkan bahwa efek tidak langsung persepsi manfaat terhadap gejala kecemasan melalui self-identification signifikan (b = 1,709; SE = 0,1055; 95% CI [1,503, 1,916]), sementara efek langsung tetap signifikan (b = 0,473; SE = 0,0922; 95% CI [0,292, 0,654]). Temuan ini mendukung adanya mediasi parsial secara statistik. Hasil penelitian mengindikasikan bahwa proses identifikasi diri dengan narasi kesehatan mental di media sosial berkaitan dengan gejala kecemasan pada remaja. Oleh karena itu, literasi kesehatan mental digital di sekolah perlu mencakup evaluasi kritis terhadap konten dan pemahaman mengenai risiko pelabelan diri.

From intention to behavioural adherence: the moderating role of eudaimonic food-related well-being orientation in Mediterranean diet adoption
abstractText: Purpose This study examines why Generation Z consumers' intentions to adopt a healthy diet do not always translate into sustained food consumption behaviour. Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB), it analyses how attitude, subjective norms and perceived behavioural control influence healthy eating intentions and how these intentions relate to self-reported adherence to the Mediterranean diet. The study also examines the moderating role of eudaimonic food-related well-being orientation in both intention formation and behavioural adherence. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 341 Generation Z consumers. Adapted multi-item scales were used to measure TPB constructs and eudaimonic food-related well-being orientation, while Mediterranean diet adherence was assessed through a dietary adherence index. Structural equation modelling was used to test direct and interaction effects. Findings Attitude and perceived behavioural control positively influence intention, whereas subjective norms do not show a significant direct effect. Perceived behavioural control and intention both positively predict self-reported adherence to the Mediterranean diet. Eudaimonic food-related well-being orientation moderates several key relationships: higher levels strengthen the effects of attitude on intention and intention on dietary adherence, while lower levels increase the influence of subjective norms and perceived behavioural control. Originality/value By conceptualising eudaimonic food-related well-being orientation as a motivational moderator, this study advances understanding of the intention–behaviour gap in healthy eating among Generation Z consumers.

title: Dysregulation of Orexin-A and Implications for Renal Function Assessment in Chronic Kidney Disease
abstractText: Abstract Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a long-standing kidney condition in which the kidneys are gradually damaged. It usually has multiple symptoms and is often accompanied by complications, such as hormonal imbalances, high blood pressure, anemia, and sleep disorders. Orexin, occasionally mentioned as hypocretin, is a neuropeptide that is mostly generated by orexin-containing neurons in the hypothalamus. Their receptors are found in a variety of tissues, such as the brain and kidney. This study aims to evaluate the impact of renal function on orexin-A levels in CKD. Materials and Methods: The study included 44 adult patients diagnosed with CKD, and their results were compared with 44 healthy participants of the same age and sex. An enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kit was used to measure orexin-A, while urea, creatinine, and lipid profile were measured using spectrophotometric methods. Association with orexin-A was performed using Pearson’s correlation analysis. Results: The results showed a significant decrease in serum orexin-A ( P < 0.001) in patients with CKD. Correlation analysis showed that orexin-A in CKD patients was positively correlated with serum creatinine ( r = 0.353, P = 0.018) and high-density lipoprotein ( r = 0.354, P = 0.017), while negatively correlated with glomerular filtration rate (GFR) ( r = −0.424, P = 0.004). Conclusions: Orexin-A levels decreased in patients with CKD, and this decrease reflects the disruption of the orexin system, which was inversely related to the GFR and directly related to creatinine and high-density lipoprotein levels.

title: Projected prevalence of hypertension and untreated/uncontrolled hypertension in Japan through 2040
abstractText: Abstract Accurate projections of future hypertension prevalence are essential for planning effective public health strategies to prevent cardiovascular mortality. This study aimed to project the future prevalence of hypertension in Japan through 2040. Prevalence estimates of hypertension and untreated/uncontrolled hypertension stratified by sex and age groups were obtained from the National Health and Nutrition Survey from 1986 to 2019. Hypertension was defined as systolic blood pressure (BP) ≥ 140 mmHg, diastolic BP ≥ 90 mmHg, or use of antihypertensive medication, and untreated/uncontrolled hypertension as systolic BP ≥ 140 mmHg or diastolic BP ≥ 90 mmHg. Three approaches were compared: a Bayesian Lee-Carter model, a model assuming monotonic prevalence change, and a constant-prevalence model. The projected prevalence estimates were applied to the population projections from the Vital Statistics of Japan. The Bayesian Lee-Carter model demonstrated the best predictive accuracy among the three models. The model projected that hypertension prevalence remained stable among men from 47.1% (95% credible interval [CI], 45.6–48.6%) in 2020 to 48.2% (44.6–52.4%) in 2040, and among women from 36.7% (35.5–37.8%) to 35.6% (32.8–38.3%). In contrast, untreated/uncontrolled hypertension prevalence would decline among men from 31.9% (28.6–34.6%) to 26.7% (18.0–38.4%), and among women from 23.1% (21.3–24.8%) to 17.2% (13.1–22.6%). The prevalence of hypertension in Japan is projected to remain largely unchanged through 2040, while the prevalence of untreated/uncontrolled hypertension is projected to decline. The findings suggest that public health policies and clinical efforts for BP control should be maintained and further strengthened to sustain and accelerate the trend.

title: When digital literacy meets negative bias: Understanding the adoption of online information and sentiment on X
abstractText: Digital platforms increasingly mediate how citizens engage with public policy, shaping not only access to information but also the formation of collective interpretations and sentiments. In the context of Indonesia’s Free Nutritious Meal (Makan Bergizi Gratis: MBG) program, this study examines the relationship between individual digital literacy and online information adoption, while simultaneously mapping public sentiment and discourse dynamics on X. Employing a concurrent mixed-methods design, the study combines an online survey of 385 social media users drawing on the DigComp 2.2 framework and the Information Adoption Model with large-scale social media analysis of 87,589 MBG-related mentions on X collected between April and August 2025 using Drone Emprit. Regression analysis revealed that digital literacy significantly predicts information adoption regarding the MBG program (β = 0.581, R² = 0.549, p < 0.001), indicating that digital literacy explains 54.9% of the variance in information adoption and substantially enhances individuals’ capacity to evaluate and accept policy-related information. While digital literacy supports information adoption at the individual level, the overall online discourse surrounding MBG remained predominantly negative, suggesting a disconnect between individual informational competence and collective sentiment formation. Sentiment analysis further revealed that public discourse was predominantly negative (56%), compared with positive (43%) and neutral (1%) expressions, with significant surges observed in May and July 2025. Network analysis additionally revealed that negative sentiment is concentrated around accounts with high centrality and influence, thereby amplifying critical narratives through networked interactions. These findings highlight a structural tension between individual informational competence and collective sentiment formation in digital communication environments. This research contributes to the existing body of work on digital communication and public policy by illustrating that initiatives aimed at improving digital literacy should be complemented by network-aware communication strategies, such as influencer engagement and real-time discourse monitoring, to bolster public trust and legitimacy in extensive policy interventions.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid positive for SARS-CoV-2 associated with neurological manifestations and proteome alterations in a multiple myeloma patient
abstractText: Abstract Background Although SARS-CoV-2 infection is primarily associated with respiratory symptoms, neurological complications have been increasingly recognized, even in the absence of pulmonary involvement. Case presentation We report a case of a 67-year-old woman with a history of multiple myeloma and recent exposure to a COVID-19-positive individual who developed rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, including dysarthria, dysphagia, and hypoesthesia, without any respiratory manifestations. Her condition deteriorated to focal and dyscognitive status epilepticus, requiring mechanical ventilation. Brain MRI showed imaging features consistent with rhombencephalitis. SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed through positive qRT-PCR results from both nasopharyngeal swab and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Further analysis of the CSF using quantitative shotgun proteomics via mass spectrometry revealed a neuroinflammatory profile indicative of blood–brain barrier disruption and differential expression of several proteins relevant to brain function, including the major prion protein, superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD-1), and other aggregation-prone proteins. Conclusions This case supports the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 can invade the central nervous system and cause severe neurological impairment, even in the absence of typical respiratory symptoms. The findings underscore the importance of considering SARS-CoV-2 in the differential diagnosis of rapidly progressive neurological syndromes and highlight the need for further investigation into the mechanisms of neuroinvasion and the potential neurotropism of emerging viral variants.

Fertility decline and population ageing in the Greater Poland Voivodeship, 2013–2024: a longitudinal analysis of implications for regional health and social services planning
abstractText: Abstract Background Persistent below-replacement fertility and population ageing are key determinants of regional health-system resilience. In Central and Eastern Europe these processes intensified after the 1990s transition, but sub-national analyses combining administrative maternity data with trend modelling remain scarce. Greater Poland offers an informative case given its demographic heterogeneity. Methods A retrospective longitudinal ecological study was conducted for 2013–2023. Two sources were analysed separately: annual live births by place of residence from Statistics Poland, used for demographic trends, and delivery records from all 34 maternity facilities (by place of delivery, stratified by perinatal reference level I–III), used for network analysis. Trends were estimated by ordinary least-squares and segmented regression. The income–birth association was assessed by Spearman correlation on levels and first differences. Sensitivity analyses excluded 2020 and restricted the facility analysis to continuously operating units. Reporting followed STROBE and RECORD. Results Live births rose from 36,561 in 2013 to a peak of 40,450 in 2017, then declined to 27,532 in 2023, a 31.9% reduction. Regression over 2017–2023 confirmed a significant decline (slope = − 2,118 births/year; 95% CI − 2,429 to − 1,807; p < 0.001; R² = 0.973). The total fertility rate fell from 1.48 in 2017 to 1.33 in 2023, against a national low of 1.099 in 2024. Between 2017 and 2023, deliveries fell by 40.3% at Level I, 30.3% at Level II and 29.2% at Level III; restricted to continuously operating units, the Level I decline was 33.0%, indicating that the larger figure reflected permanent closure of four peripheral units rather than a disproportionately greater fall in demand. Income showed no significant association with births on levels (ρ = −0.370; p = 0.293) or after first-differencing (ρ = 0.167; p = 0.668). Conclusions Greater Poland experienced a sustained decline in live births between 2013 and 2023, distributed broadly evenly across perinatal reference levels, while the delivery network contracted disproportionately through closure of peripheral Level I units. The data did not support an independent income–fertility association once the common time trend was removed. The findings bear on adaptive perinatal network planning and geriatric-care expansion, and represent planning implications rather than tested outcomes.

Tumor microenvironment-driven therapeutic resistance in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
abstractText: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most treatment-refractory malignancies, with limited and often transient benefit from chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and radiotherapy. Therapeutic resistance is increasingly recognized as an ecosystem-level process arising from reciprocal interactions between malignant cells and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Dense extracellular matrix, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs), dysfunctional vasculature, immunosuppressive myeloid and lymphoid populations, hypoxic niches, metabolic networks, microbiota, extracellular vesicles (EVs), and neural components collectively restrict drug delivery and promote adaptive survival, immune escape, stemness, and treatment-induced evolution. This review integrates these processes into a PDAC resistance ecosystem framework. We discuss how stromal remodeling, hypoxia-driven adaptation, metabolic-immune crosstalk, extracellular communication, cancer stem cell plasticity, and TME-regulated autophagy and ferroptosis contribute to resistance across therapeutic modalities. We further evaluate emerging strategies involving stromal reprogramming, myeloid and immune remodeling, metabolic intervention, hypoxia targeting, and regulated cell-death sensitization. Particular emphasis is placed on the limited clinical translation of indiscriminate stromal depletion and single-target approaches. Finally, we propose that spatial multi-omics, longitudinal biomarker profiling, and adaptive combination therapy will be required to identify dominant resistance programs and guide patient-specific intervention in PDAC.

Benefits of Active Noise Canceling to Prevent Excessive Noise Exposure Via Personal Listening Devices
abstractText: Background and Objectives The use of personal listening devices (PLDs), particularly wireless earbuds, has increased substantially, raising concerns about noise-induced hearing loss as users often raise volumes in noisy environments. Many recent earbuds are equipped with active noise canceling (ANC) technology. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of ANC in four popular wireless earbud models using both subjective and objective methods in simulated noisy conditions.Subjects and Method A total of 47 participants with normal hearing completed listening tests each using the earbud under ANC ON and ANC OFF conditions. Preferred listening levels (PLLs) were obtained under bus and café noise conditions, and real-ear measurements (REMs) were obtained under bus noise. Two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to compare PLLs and REMs across ANC conditions and earbud types.Results Significant interaction effects between earbud type and ANC status were observed for both PLLs (p<0.001 in bus noise; p=0.003 in café noise) and REMs (p<0.001 at low and whole frequencies; p<0.001 at high frequencies). Among the four models, earbuds C and D showed greatest reductions in both volume levels and ambient noise.Conclusion Although ANC performance varied slightly between models, overall, ANC was effective in reducing PLLs and real-ear sound levels in noisy environments. These findings suggest that ANC-equipped wireless earbuds may help reduce potential sound exposure during PLD use; however, further longitudinal studies with audiometric outcomes are needed to determine whether these reductions translate into long-term hearing protection.

title: AI as Co-Designer and Feedback Partner: Enhancing Human Judgment
abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) is shaping the future of higher education, tasking educators with transforming teaching, learning, and assessment practices to consider how AI can enhance the educational environment. With its increasing availability, it is important for administrators, faculty, and students to explore the practical nature of AI use prior to entry into the workforce. Faculty must also reevaluate how they approach assessing student learning, tasking them to rethink each assessment’s purpose, how it will inform future practice, and how it will prepare learners to use AI. Furthermore, faculty must also be prepared to consider the collaborative nature of AI, transforming their mindset to consider AI as an active co-designer and partner, one that does not seek to diminish the educator’s human judgment. This manuscript will articulate the importance of co-design, where AI and educators collaboratively shape assessment tools, and serve to champion feedback partnerships that enhance reflective practice for both students and faculty.

abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Influencer Marketing dan Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) terhadap Impulsive Buying di TikTok Shop pada Generasi Z di RT 03 RW 03 Cinere, Kota Depok. Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda dengan bantuan SPSS versi 25. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Influencer Marketing berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Impulsive Buying, ditunjukkan oleh nilai t-hitung (5,374) > t-tabel (2,000) dan nilai signifikansi (0,000 < 0,05). Dengan demikian, peningkatan Influencer Marketing dan Fear of Missing Out (FOMO) dapat meningkatkan Impulsive Buying di TikTok Shop pada Generasi Z.

title: Virtuality and Ludicity: Narrative Experimentation in The Merchant and the Alchemist’s Gate
abstractText: The Merchant and the Alchemist’s Gate is a narrative experiment. Time travel, as a traditional science fiction theme, is often mediated by a time machine to traverse between the real world and the past or future, with the real world serving as both the starting point and destination, highlighting the subjectivity and reversibility between different times and spaces. But in The Merchant and the Alchemist’s Gate, the time travel breaks out of the conventional form of science fiction, turning time travel into irreversible one-dimensional behavior and becoming a virtual reality game-like narrative experiment. This paper puts traditional time travel into the background of digital age, reveals the fuzzy treatment of fictional world and real world in ontology dimension through the operation logic of virtual game, discusses the virtual and game nature of real world in the novel at ontology level, and examines how alchemist’s gate becomes a metaphorical expression in digital age.

Association Between Neighbourhood-level Antibiotic Utilization and the Rate of Community-Associated C. difficile (CA-CDI) Infection: An Ecological Study
abstractText: Abstract Background Despite reductions in hospital-associated Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) incidence in Canada and the United States, the incidence of community-associated CDI (CA-CDI) has remained high. We sought to investigate whether neighbourhood-level variation in antibiotic utilization is associated with CA-CDI. Method We conducted a neighbourhood-level ecological study across 1,520 neighbourhoods in Ontario, Canada. Residents aged ≥66 without hospitalization in the prior 30 days were eligible for inclusion from 2017 to 2023. Antibiotic utilization, CDI cases, and population were identified for each neighbourhood using comprehensive province-wide databases. CA-CDI rate was the outcome (incident cases of CA-CDI/10,000 person-years). Rate of antibiotic utilization (DOT per 1000 person-days) was the primary exposure. The rate-ratio (RR) of CA-CDI associated with increased antibiotic utilization was estimated using negative-binomial regression, adjusting for 8 demographic and health care covariates. We also evaluated risk based on low-, moderate-, and high-risk antibiotic strata based on published literature. Result We identified 19,757 CA-CDI cases. We observed substantial variation in antibiotic utilization across neighbourhoods (Median=21.1 DOT/1000 person-days; interquartile range [IQR], 16.7–25.6). After adjustments, we observed an association between overall antibiotic utilization (RR=1.13 per 10-point increase in DOT; 95% confidence interval [95%CI], 1.09–1.18). A gradient wherein higher risk antibiotic agents were more strongly associated with CA-CDI was apparent (Low-risk: RR=1.08; 95%CI, 1.01–1.15; Moderate-risk: RR=1.27; 95%CI, 1.15–1.39; High-risk: RR=1.73; 95%CI, 1.13–2.66). Discussion Neighbourhoods with higher antibiotic utilization, especially for moderate and high-risk antibiotics, have higher CA-CDI incidence. Reducing variability in neighbourhood antibiotic utilization could help reduce the burden of CDI.

Platelet Indices as Biomarkers of Disease Severity and Morbidity in Hospitalized Dengue Patients
abstractText: Abstract Background: Dengue fever is a rapidly expanding mosquito-borne illness with significant morbidity in children. While thrombocytopenia is a key feature, platelet count alone poorly predicts disease severity. Platelet indices such as mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), and plateletcrit (PCT) may provide better insight into disease progression and complications. Materials and Methods: This hospital-based cross-sectional observational study was conducted in the Department of Pediatrics, at a tertiary care hospital over 18 months. A total of 120 children aged 1–16 years with confirmed dengue infection (NS1 antigen or immunoglobulin M positive) were enrolled. Platelet indices were recorded at admission. Patients were classified according to the World Health Organization 2009 dengue severity criteria. Associations between platelet indices and disease severity, hepatic dysfunction, and renal dysfunction were analyzed using appropriate statistical tests. Results: Among 120 patients, 35% had dengue without warning signs, 48.3% had warning signs, and 16.7% had severe dengue. MPV and PCT decreased, while PDW increased significantly with disease severity ( P < 0.001). Hepatic (31.7%) and renal (9.2%) dysfunction were associated with lower MPV and PCT and higher PDW ( P < 0.001). PDW showed a strong positive correlation with severity ( r = 0.71), whereas MPV and PCT showed negative correlations. Conclusion: Platelet indices, particularly PDW and PCT, are simple, readily available, and reliable markers for predicting disease severity and organ dysfunction in pediatric dengue. Their routine use may aid early risk stratification, timely intervention, and improved clinical decision-making, especially in resource-limited settings where advanced biomarkers may not be accessible.

title: Distribusi Spasial Kejadian Tuberkulosis Resistan Obat di Provinsi Sumatera Barat Tahun 2020-2024
abstractText: Tuberkulosis resistan obat (TB-RO) masih menjadi tantangan dalam pengendalian tuberkulosis karena penanganannya lebih kompleks dan dapat menunjukkan distribusi yang berbeda antarwilayah. Pendekatan spasial diperlukan untuk mengidentifikasi pola persebaran dan wilayah yang berpotensi membentuk klaster kasus sebagai informasi dalam penentuan prioritas pengendalian. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendistribusikan pola spasial kejadian TB-RO di Provinsi Sumatera Barat tahun 2020–2024. Penelitian menggunakan desain studi ekologi dengan data sekunder kejadian TB-RO pada kabupaten/kota yang diperoleh dari Dinas Kesehatan Provinsi Sumatera Barat. Analisis spasial dilakukan menggunakan Global Moran’s I untuk mengidentifikasi autokorelasi spasial secara global dan Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA) untuk mengidentifikasi klaster dan outlier spasial lokal. Selama tahun 2020–2024 tercatat 499 kasus TB-RO, dengan kasus tertinggi ditemukan di Kota Padang sebanyak 128 kasus. Analisis kumulatif tahun 2020–2024 menghasilkan Moran’s I sebesar 0,053 (p=0,210), yang menunjukkan tidak terdapat autokorelasi spasial global yang signifikan. Analisis LISA mengidentifikasi Kabupaten Padang Pariaman sebagai wilayah High-High (hotspot), sedangkan Kota Solok termasuk Low-High sebagai outlier spasial lokal. Kejadian TB-RO di Provinsi Sumatera Barat tidak menunjukkan pengelompokan spasial yang signifikan secara global, tetapi ditemukan variasi dan pengelompokan secara lokal. Pemodelan spasial dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai informasi pendukung dalam menentukan wilayah prioritas untuk penguatan surveilans, penemuan kasus, investigasi kontak, dan pengendalian TB-RO.

title: Multimorbidity Burden and Specific Clinical Comorbidities in Onychomycosis: A Retrospective Case-Control Study in an Indonesian Tertiary Referral Hospital
abstractText: Background: Onychomycosis is the most common chronic fungal disease of the nail unit worldwide. Metabolic, vascular and cutaneous disorders are known risk factors. The added effect of a combined comorbidity burden in tropical outpatient populations remains under-evaluated. Objective: To describe the spectrum of clinical comorbidities and to analyze the association between cumulative comorbidity burden and onychomycosis among outpatients of a tertiary referral hospital in Indonesia. Methods: This retrospective case-control study took place at the Dermatology Clinic of Dr. Moewardi General Hospital, Surakarta (January 2020 to June 2026). It enrolled 76 patients. There were 38 mycologically confirmed onychomycosis cases (positive 10% potassium hydroxide mount and/or culture) and 38 outpatient controls without onychomycosis. We recorded demographics, obesity, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, venous insufficiency, psoriasis, HIV/immunosuppression, systemic autoimmune disease, tinea pedis and the total comorbidity count. Bivariate analyses used the chi-square and Fisher exact tests. We calculated odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results: Tinea pedis (47.4%), obesity (39.5%), hypertension (36.8%), autoimmune disease (31.6%) and diabetes mellitus (31.6%) were the most common comorbidities among cases. Multimorbidity (≥2 comorbidities) was more frequent in cases than in controls (50.0% vs. 15.8%). Patients with no comorbidity were mostly controls (28.9% vs. 7.9%). Cumulative comorbidity burden was associated with onychomycosis (chi-square = 12.01, p = 0.002). The OR for ≥2 vs. 0 comorbidities was 11.61 (95% CI: 2.41–55.94, p = 0.002). Conclusion: A higher cumulative comorbidity burden was associated with onychomycosis in this single-center case-control study. Management should address coexisting metabolic, vascular and fungal-reservoir conditions alongside antifungal treatment.

title: Tetronarce ramanamurthyi sp. nov. (Torpediniformes: Torpedinidae), a new species of electric ray from the southeastern Arabian Sea, northern Indian Ocean
abstractText: A new species of electric ray, Tetronarce ramanamurthyi sp. nov., is described based on nine specimens collected from the deepwaters off the southeastern Arabian Sea , northern Indian Ocean. T. ramanamurthyi sp. nov. is characterised by uniform dark bluish black or dark brown dorsal colouration and absence of papillae around the spiracles and can be distinguished from its congeners by a combination of characters: disc wider than disc length, disc length 1.0–1.2 in disc width; relatively large endolymphatic pore (1.2–1.6% TL), spiracle nearly equal to eye, spiracle oval shaped, short interspiracular distance (4.1–5.5% TL), larger spiracles (spiracle length 3.9–5.1% TL) and smaller electric organs 23.3–28.9% TL in length and 10.6–13.8% TL in maximum width. Vertebral counts totalled 99, comprising 30 monospondylous and 69 diplospondylous centra. T. ramanamurthyi sp. nov. is so far known only from the southeastern Arabian Sea, and represents the first confirmed record of Tetronarce species from the northern Indian Ocean.

title: Microplastic contamination in surface water and sediments of Lake Canaçari, Central Amazon, during the dry season
abstractText: Abstract Contamination by microplastics is an emerging environmental problem that is widely distributed across continental aquatic environments and may cause ecological impacts. This study evaluated the occurrence, concentration, and chemical and morphological characteristics of microplastics in surface waters and sediments from Lake Canaçari, comparing two areas with different land-use patterns within a floodplain system in the Central Amazon. Microplastics were detected in all sampled areas. In surface water, concentrations ranged from 0 (no microplastic particles detected in one sample) to 1,000 microplastics·m⁻ 3 (405 ± 298 microplastics·m⁻ 3 ), while in sediments, they ranged from 7 to 307 microplastics·kg⁻ 1 (77 ± 104 microplastics·kg⁻ 1 ). No significant differences in microplastic concentrations were observed between fishing and human-settlement areas. The particles were predominantly blue fibers (< 1,000 μm). Among the spectroscopically analyzed particles, polyethylene was the most frequently identified polymer, while copper phthalocyanine pigments, including Pigment Blue 15 and Pigment Green 7, were also detected by FTIR and/or Raman spectroscopy. Overall, the results suggest that Lake Canaçari may act as a transport pathway, redistribution zone, and retention compartment for microplastics; however, seasonal sampling is needed to confirm how these processes vary throughout the hydrological cycle. These results reinforce the role of Amazonian floodplain systems in the regional dynamics of microplastics and highlight the need for monitoring and management strategies that incorporate seasonal hydrological connectivity at the basin scale.

title: Accuracy of transfer learning in predicting peri-implantitis onset from intraoral radiograph: A multi-center longitudinal retrospective study
abstractText: Abstract Background The growing application of artificial intelligence in dentistry has opened new opportunities for predicting peri-implantitis (PI) using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Transfer learning, where knowledge from a model pre-trained on a large dataset is adapted to a new, domain-specific task, may enhance performance, particularly when medical datasets are limited. This study evaluated the ability of several pre-trained CNN architectures applied to baseline 2D intraoral radiographs to predict peri-implantitis onset. Methods A retrospective multi-center study was conducted at the University of Michigan and King’s College London. A total of 195 implants (146 from Michigan and 49 from London) placed in 108 maintained patients were included. For each implant, a baseline periapical radiograph taken up to one year after prosthetic restoration was analyzed. Five pre-trained CNN architectures (ResNet50, DenseNet, VGG16, InceptionV3, EfficientNet) were combined with four transfer learning strategies: feature extraction (hybrid and non-hybrid), partial fine-tuning (50% of layers), and full fine-tuning. Models were trained using patient-wise splits to avoid leakage, and performance was evaluated on an independent test set using accuracy, area under the ROC curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. Results All CNN architectures showed variable performance across transfer learning strategies. The non-hybrid feature extraction approach provided the most consistent discrimination, with the best models achieving AUC values between 0.74 and 0.83. InceptionV3 reached the highest AUC (0.83). Fine-tuning strategies yielded modest or low performance, with AUCs generally ranging from 0.42 to 0.69 across architectures. Conclusion Non-hybrid feature extraction applied to pre-trained CNNs showed the most promising, though moderate, performance for predicting PI onset from baseline intraoral radiographs. These findings indicate that transfer learning may assist early risk stratification in implant dentistry, but larger prospective studies are needed before clinical adoption. Clinical relevance Deep learning models may serve as adjunctive tools to identify implants at higher risk for future PI based on routine baseline radiographs, supporting more individualized maintenance protocols and earlier preventive interventions.

Talquetamab and Its Effect on Relapsed and Refractory Multiple Myeloma
abstractText: Abstract Relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) remains a challenging condition despite many advances in immunotherapies. Outcomes are particularly dismal in patients who are refractory to these three major classes of proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapies. Novel bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) have shown some promising efficacy in heavily pretreated patients, even those with triple‐ and penta‐refractory disease. Talquetamab is a BsAb recently approved for the treatment of relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma. Talquetamab demonstrated a high overall response rate of approximately 70%, including in patients that are previously treated with T‐cell therapies. The safety profile of talquetamab is consistent with other BsAbs, with similar adverse events. The efficacy of talquetamab and other therapies, including CAR‐T cell treatments, remains an area of active research, as resistance to anti‐B-cell maturation antigen therapies poses a clinical challenge. Current trials are exploring the use of talquetamab in combination therapies. There is now adequate data to further support talquetamab’s efficacy, making it a very important addition to the RRMM treatment domain.
