Research on E -Commerce Cross -Border Automotive Event -Marketing in the Attention -Economy Era— A Case Study of the JD -GAC Blind -Bid Sky -High -Price Vehicle Campaign
abstractText: Against the backdrop of digital-real integration and fierce homogenised competition in the new-energy-vehicle (NEV) industry, traditional marketing approaches suffer high customer-acquisition costs. This paper takes the JD-GAC "1-yuan Blind-bid for a National-Favourite Car" campaign as a case to explore e-commerce cross-border event marketing under the attention-economy theory. It analyses topic design, traffic channels, user operation and multi-party brand endorsement, and identifies core drivers for its phenomenal communication effect: disruptive interactive gameplay, low-threshold mass participation, joint brand endorsement and full-domain digital dissemination. The study reveals major marketing pain points of domestic NEV brands and extracts practical suggestions covering communication strategy, channel construction, user management, product planning and risk control. Findings indicate that suspense-oriented e-commerce event marketing can achieve low-cost brand exposure. Nevertheless, automakers must build online-offline service closed-loops and convert short-term viral traffic into sustainable sales and brand reputation. This research provides empirical references for NEV manufacturers to carry out digital cross-border marketing activities.

title: AI-Assisted Sentiment Analysis of Student Voice: A Human-Validated Comparison of Lexicon and Transformer-Based Tools
abstractText: Open-ended survey responses offer rich insights into the student experience, yet analyzing this qualitative data at scale is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. This study evaluates whether off-the-shelf sentiment analysis tools can validly classify such data for institutional assessment. Analyzing 1,220 free-text responses from undergraduate students at a private liberal arts university, we compared the performance of four tools: two lexicon-based (TextBlob and VADER) and two transformer-based (BERT-nlptown and RoBERTa-cardiffnlp) against manual coding. Evaluation metrics included accuracy, macro F1 score, and Cohen’s kappa (κ). While BERT-nlptown performed best, it achieved only moderate agreement with human coding (κ = .42). Furthermore, lexicon-based approaches misclassified roughly 20% of responses due to limited vocabulary coverage. Notably, all tools struggled to accurately classify negative, neutral and mixed sentiments. We recommend conducting lexicon-coverage diagnostics, few-shot prompting, domain-specific finetuning, and human-in-the-loop oversight to ensure valid, reliable, and trustworthy institutional assessment.

title: Malocclusion and orthodontic treatment needs among individuals with down syndrome in Egypt: a multicentre cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background Individuals with Down syndrome commonly present with a variety of craniofacial and dental anomalies that increase the prevalence of malocclusion and the need for orthodontic treatment. Despite this, data regarding orthodontic needs in this population in the middle east, particularly in Egypt, remain limited. Aim of the study This study aimed to assess the patterns of malocclusion and orthodontic treatment needs among individuals with Down syndrome. Materials and methods A total of 117 individuals with Down syndrome aged 12–25 years, who met the study’s eligibility criteria, were recruited from specialized institutions in Egypt in a multi-centred cross-sectional study. Clinical examination included extraoral and intraoral assessment, occlusal analysis using Angle’s classification, and assessment of the need for orthodontic treatment using Dental Health Component of Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need (IOTN). Additional data on oral hygiene, oral habits, and craniofacial features were recorded. Descriptive statistics were computed for all study variables. Qualitative (categorical) variables were presented as frequencies (n) and percentages (%). Results Class I molar relationship was the most common (41.0%), followed by Class II (29.9%) and Class III (29.1%). Anterior open bite (23.1%) and posterior crossbite (21.4%) were also frequently observed. Regarding orthodontic treatment need, 71.7% of participants demonstrated borderline to very great need (IOTN Grades 3–5), with 49.6% exhibiting great or very great need (Grades 4–5). Fair or poor oral hygiene was identified in 81.2% of participants. Mouth breathing was the most common oral habit (32.5%). Conclusion Patients with Down syndrome exhibit a high prevalence of malocclusion and a significant need for orthodontic treatment. Early orthodontic assessment, preventive strategies, and multidisciplinary management are essential to improve oral health outcomes in this population. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: The synthesis of sulfonyl fluoride functionalised tetrasubstituted thiophenes using a diversity oriented clicking approach
abstractText: We present a diversity-oriented clicking (DOC) approach for the synthesis of a library of novel clickable, highly functionalised thiophenes that serve as versatile hubs for sulfur fluoride exchange (SuFEx) click chemistry diversification. Using 2-substituted-alkynyl-1-sulfonyl fluorides (SASFs) as DOC connectors, we investigated their reactivity with zwitterionic pyridinium thiolates to selectively access two classes of sulfur-containing heterocycles, namely pyridothiazepines and thiophenes, as SuFExable heterocyclic hubs. However, due to the instability of the pyridothiazepine products, our efforts were redirected toward the selective synthesis and isolation of the thiophene products. Accordingly, 12 highly functionalised SuFExable thiophenes were isolated in yields of up to 87%. The transformation is straightforward to perform, tolerates a broad range of functional groups and proceeds under mild reaction conditions. The potential for diversification of the thiophene scaffold was further demonstrated through SuFEx click chemistry.

Assessment Professionals’ Journey to Owning GenAI Adoption
abstractText: This Special Issue started with a question - what can assessment practitioners do to optimize GenAI adoption across contexts? While GenAI is no longer considered passing or irrelevant in assessment work, scholarly sharing of its applications have been primarily bound to the classroom assessment context. Professionals have, and must continue to, build knowledge and skill in navigating the GenAI to maintain momentum in relentlessly pursuing continuous improvement within their institutions, whether they are encouraging and seeking rapid integration or more cautiously approaching these technological breakthroughs. The articles in this Special Issue take GenAI implementation from integration on the margins and in the classroom only to being embraced with intentionality across the institution. Through stories of practice, basic research, and frameworks, they focus on way that the assessment practitioner can own GenAI adoption, expanding the conversation. Practitioners can walk away with a perspective shift on GenAI- from a potential threat to a willing partner.

title: Pelatihan Google Docs sebagai Media Kolaborasi Digital di SMKN 1 Banjarmasin
abstractText: Google Docs is a cloud-based word processing application from Google that enables users to create, edit, and collaborate on documents in real-time. The service allows multiple users to work on the same document simultaneously, making it a highly effective tool for collaboration in an educational setting. Google manages a secure server infrastructure, ensuring that users can access their documents anytime and anywhere—via public or private internet networks—using a variety of devices. This training aims to enhance students' digital skills in utilizing collaborative tools to support academic activities and group assignments at SMKN 1 Banjarmasin. The program was implemented in three main stages: a preparation phase involving a needs analysis; an implementation phase consisting of material presentation and hands-on document collaboration practice; and an evaluation phase. The results indicate an improvement in the participants' understanding and technical proficiency regarding Google Docs' collaborative features, such as managing sharing permissions, co-editing, and using the commenting function. This training is expected to foster a more structured, efficient, and flexible culture of group collaboration within the school environment.

title: SUPERVISI AKADEMIK, KOMPETENSI PROFESIONAL, DAN ORGANISASI SEKOLAH DALAM MENINGKATKAN KINERJA GURU SEKOLAH DASAR
abstractText: ABSTRACT Elementary school teacher performance is associated with instructional quality and is influenced by various professional and institutional factors. Therefore, examining the relationships among academic supervision, professional competence, and school organization is necessary to understand the factors associated with teacher performance. This study aimed to analyze the relationships of these three variables with the performance of public elementary school teachers in Pringgasela District, East Lombok Regency, both individually and simultaneously. A quantitative approach with an ex post facto correlational design was employed. The study population consisted of 256 teachers, from which 156 respondents were selected using proportional random sampling. Data were collected through Likert-scale questionnaires supported by observation and documentation, then analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics 26. The results revealed that academic supervision, professional competence, and school organization were each positively and significantly associated with teacher performance. Simultaneously, the regression model was statistically significant, with an R² value of 0.816, indicating that the three predictors explained 81.6% of the variation in teacher performance within the sample. Professional competence had the largest standardized beta coefficient among the three predictors. These findings suggest that teacher performance development should integrate professional competence enhancement, academic supervision, and organizational support while also considering other factors beyond the scope of the model. ABSTRAK Kinerja guru sekolah dasar berkaitan dengan kualitas pembelajaran dan dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor profesional maupun kelembagaan. Oleh karena itu, keterkaitan supervisi akademik, kompetensi profesional, dan organisasi sekolah perlu dikaji secara terpadu untuk memperoleh gambaran mengenai faktor-faktor yang berhubungan dengan kinerja guru. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan ketiga variabel tersebut dengan kinerja guru Sekolah Dasar Negeri di Kecamatan Pringgasela, Kabupaten Lombok Timur, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain ex post facto korelasional. Populasi penelitian berjumlah 256 guru, dengan sampel sebanyak 156 responden yang dipilih melalui teknik proportional random sampling. Data diperoleh melalui kuesioner berskala Likert, didukung observasi dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif dan regresi linear berganda dengan IBM SPSS Statistics 26. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa supervisi akademik, kompetensi profesional, dan organisasi sekolah masing-masing berhubungan positif dan signifikan dengan kinerja guru. Secara simultan, model regresi signifikan dengan nilai R² sebesar 0,816, yang berarti ketiga prediktor menjelaskan 81,6% variasi kinerja guru dalam sampel. Kompetensi profesional memiliki koefisien beta terstandarisasi terbesar dibandingkan kedua prediktor lainnya. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa pengembangan kinerja guru perlu memperhatikan kompetensi profesional, pembinaan akademik, dan dukungan organisasi secara terpadu, tanpa mengabaikan faktor lain di luar model penelitian.

abstractText: This study aims to describe individual psychological characteristics and components of the psychographic profiles of residents of Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug– Yugra and Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug with a history of unlawful behaviour. The study was conducted in 2022 and included 418 participants aged 17–45 years, comprising 220 women and 198 men. The assessment used the Rogers–Dymond Social-Psychological Adaptation Questionnaire, Boyko’s emotionality assessment method, and selected items from Raven’s Standard Progressive Matrices. Correlation and exploratory factor analyses are reported. Maladaptation was positively associated with external control, escapism, submissiveness, and emotional discomfort. The first three factors jointly accounted for 50.96% of the variance and reflected maladaptation, the balance between acceptance and rejection of oneself and others, and internal control and adaptability. The findings may inform hypothesis development and individualised psychological support programmes; they do not establish the causes of unlawful behaviour.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Financial Accounting Efficiency and the Continued Importance of Human Oversight
abstractText: This paper mainly examines whether artificial intelligence (AI) can really improve the efficiency of financial accounting work, and why accountants are still required to verify its outputs and provide necessary supervision. To address these issues, this study reviews academic papers and reports published by professional institutions. Based on these studies, AI has been shown to perform repetitive tasks that follow fixed procedures. In addition, it can process large volumes of transactions, detect potential errors, and use historical data to forecast future sales or cash flows. Thus, AI reduces the time accountants spend on manual processing, thereby enabling them to allocate more time to analyzing financial information and generating valuable business insights. However, if the data provided by the company is incorrect or incomplete, the results may also be inaccurate. Moreover, financial records may contain private information, such as bank details, employee salaries, and customer data. As a result, AI should assist accountants rather than replace them. In this process, accountants still need to verify AI-generated results, review relevant information, make judgments based on the company's actual situation, and take responsibility for final decisions.

title: Development of Communication Styles Scale (CSS) for University Students: Qualitative Item Generation and Content Validation
abstractText: University life is one of the most challenging phases of a student's life because of the interplay of social and academic demands, resulting in anxiety and stress (Yan, 2025; Zhang et al., 2022; SAMFIRA, 2020). One of the challenges is maintaining good interpersonal relationships and communication is imperative to this (Horan et al., 2021, Griggio et al., 2019; Chandra, Mohammadnezhad, & Ward, 2018). However, as people vary both in verbal and non-verbal communication due to cultural differences (Mascarenhas et al., 2015); it is important to know more about this area to develop effective communication skills accordingly. The current study aimed to develop a scale to measure communication styles among university students. Following a rigorous literature review, which identified gaps in existing measures, two focus groups and three semi-structured interviews with clinical psychologists were conducted. After thematic analysis, a final pool of items was generated for expert review. For this, Content Validity Index was established by clinical psychologists through rating the relevance of the items to the construct (N=7) and 40 items were retained.

title: Predicting Passing-Play Outcomes in American Football: A Comparative Study of Traditional Machine Learning Algorithms and Fine-Tuned Large Language Models
abstractText: This study examines American football passing play strategies based on an analysis of 100 NFL games, addressing the notable lack of research on offensive passing strategies. The yardage prediction task is formulated as a regression task, and the touchdown prediction task is formulated as a classification task. A regression analysis was conducted using four traditional machine learning models, including Support Vector Machines (SVMs), K-Nearest Neighbors, XGBoost, and LightGBM, and a LoRA-fine-tuned Llama 3 (8B) model. The SVM model showed optimal performance with a Mean Absolute Error of 6.996 yards, marginally outperforming the Llama 3 model (7.059 yards). In contrast, the fine-tuned Llama 3 significantly outperformed all traditional algorithms for the classification task, with a Macro F1 of 0.712 compared to the highest Macro F1 of 0.614 for traditional algorithms. Therefore, I advocate large language models (LLMs) for classification tasks and traditional machine learning algorithms for regression tasks. Sports analytics models can be selected based on the findings of these studies.

Three-Dimensional Numerical Modelling of an Existing Hollow Lining as an Unintentional Vibration Barrier for Metro-Induced Ground and Building Vibrations
abstractText: Metro-induced ground and building vibrations pose a significant environmental concern in dense urban areas. Conventional prediction methods assume homogeneous soil and overlook the wave modulation effect of large artificial cavities such as utility tunnels, causing notable deviations from field measurements. This study develops a three-dimensional coupled finite element model integrating vehicle-track dynamics and a tunnel-soil-building system, with a circular hollow lining between the tunnel and building to represent existing large-diameter cavities. Parametric analyses quantify the effects of lining diameter, burial depth, and concrete strength. The results reveal a universal spatial zoning effect: vibrations increase by 2%–14% on the tunnel side due to incident-reflected wave superposition, and decrease by 20%–51% on the building side due to wave shielding. Lining diameter is the dominant factor, providing 2.2–2.3 dB additional reduction per 1 m increase. Concrete strength yields limited benefits, while burial depth uniquely regulates vibration energy distribution. The influence weight ranks as diameter > concrete strength > burial depth. The 5 m case provides a 9 dB safety margin for the building. These findings clarify the unintentional shielding effect of existing cavities and can guide metro vibration assessment and underground space planning.

Plantas medicinales, autoatención y salud bucal: patrimonio biocultural campesino en una comunidad rural de Antioquia, Colombia
abstractText: En América Latina, las prácticas comunitarias de autoatención con plantas medicinales para el cuidado de la salud bucal permanecen escasamente comprendidas, en un contexto donde persisten jerarquías epistémicas que deslegitiman estos saberes y donde el patrimonio biocultural que los sustenta se encuentra en riesgo de erosión. Este estudio exploró las prácticas de autoatención con plantas medicinales para el cuidado de la salud bucal en la comunidad campesina de la vereda Pantanillo, municipio de San Pedro de los Milagros, Antioquia, Colombia, entre mayo y septiembre de 2025. Mediante un enfoque etnográfico, se integraron observación participante, entrevistas semiestructuradas a 19 participantes, notas de campo y fotovoz. El análisis identificó cuatro categorías: salud como equilibrio y autonomía terapéutica, saber heredado y practicado en la relación cotidiana con las plantas, erosiones y persistencias del patrimonio biocultural, y plantas medicinales y salud bucal. Se documentaron 14 plantas con usos específicos en salud bucal para el manejo del dolor, la inflamación y la cicatrización. Los hallazgos muestran que la autoatención constituye un sistema de conocimiento con racionalidad propia, dentro del cual las plantas medicinales son uno de los recursos terapéuticos sustentado en criterios locales de dosificación, selección de especies y transmisión intergeneracional que se articula con la biomedicina en itinerarios terapéuticos híbridos.

title: Preparation of Composite Flocculants Using Poly Aluminum Chloride, Polyacrylamide, and Copper Oxide Loaded on Oyster Shells for Wastewater Treatment
abstractText: As living standards continue to rise, people have increasingly higher demands for water quantity and quality. As vital water sources, the methods and efficiency of pollutant removal from rivers, lakes, and reservoirs are of paramount importance. This study prepared a multifunctional wastewater treatment material by loading polyaluminum chloride (PAC), polyacrylamide (PAM), and copper oxide (CuO) onto oyster shell (Os) powder. This material integrates adsorption, coagulation, and antibacterial functions. Its coagulation and antibacterial performance were investigated, and the fractal dimension and particle size distribution of the flocs formed after coagulation were studied. Results indicate that both turbidity removal efficiency and total phosphorus removal efficiency exhibit an initial increase followed by a decrease with rising dosage of PPCO composite material and experimental temperature. After coagulation treatment of raw water samples with 40 mg/L 12-PPCO composite material, turbidity and total phosphorus removal rates reached 86.21% and 60.51%, respectively, while inhibition rates against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus were 98.93% and 98.12%. This study achieved resource utilization of oyster shells while significantly enhancing wastewater treatment efficiency, offering a novel approach for improving water quality in rivers and lakes.

abstractText: This practitioner inquiry reports on a pilot at a small Catholic liberal arts college that used generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-supported tools to help faculty complete program-assessment documentation during a structured Education Day. Grounded in Catholic social teaching and human-centered AI principles, the pilot tested a framework organized around human judgment, ethical stewardship, and formative human-AI partnership. Survey results from the pilot cohort (N = 10; item-level valid responses varied) showed strong faculty endorsement, including unanimous agreement that the process deepened thinking about evidence of student learning and unanimous intent to use AI-supported tools in future cycles. Qualitative findings identified five themes: efficiency and cognitive scaffolding, human-in-the-loop validation, platform reliability and trust, data governance, and institutional support infrastructure. Findings suggest that mission-driven institutions can integrate AI into assessment responsibly when faculty formation, verification checkpoints, and governance structures precede broad implementation.

Inteligencia artificial y desempeño laboral del personal administrativo en una universidad Pública en la Ciudad de Trujillo, 2024
abstractText: El estudio tuvo como propósito determinar la relación entre el uso de la inteligencia artificial y el desempeño laboral del personal administrativo en una Universidad Pública de la ciudad de Trujillo, 2024. Se desarrolló a partir de un enfoque cuantitativo, siendo este de tipo aplicado, con nivel correlacional y diseño no experimental de tipo transversal. En la población participaron 884 servidores administrativos de los que se obtuvo una muestra de 128 servidores mediante muestreo probabilístico aleatorio simple. Se aplicaron dos cuestionarios con escala tipo Likert para medir ambas variables. La confiabilidad de los instrumentos, calculada mediante el alfa de Cronbach, tuvo valores de 0,791 y 0,778, que evidencian una adecuada consistencia interna. El procesamiento de la información se realizó empleando SPSS versión 27, aplicando estadística descriptiva e inferencial. Los resultados indicaron una correlación positiva muy alta y significativa (Rho = 0,795; p < 0,01), lo que indica que mientras mayor sea el uso de la inteligencia artificial, mejor será el desempeño laboral. En función de lo anterior, se concluye que la inteligencia artificial constituye un recurso estratégico para incrementar la eficiencia, la productividad y la calidad del trabajo, resaltando la importancia de continuar trabajando los aspectos de las competencias digitales en la universidad.

title: The Association of Duration of Yoga Practice on the Physiological and Cardiopulmonary Variables
abstractText: Abstract Background: Yoga is a holistic practice linked with various physiological and cardiopulmonary benefits. However, the relationship between the duration of yoga practice and these parameters remains insufficiently explored. Objectives: To assess the association between the duration of yoga practice and selected anthropometric, cardiovascular, and respiratory parameters among healthy adults. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional study included 100 healthy adults who practiced yoga for at least 30 min per day on a minimum of 4 days per week. Participants were classified into two groups according to the duration of yoga practice: <6 months ( n = 50) and >6 months ( n = 50). Anthropometric and cardiopulmonary parameters were assessed and compared between the groups. Results: Participants practicing yoga for >6 months had significantly lower body weight, body mass index, waist circumference, hip circumference, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and heart rate compared with those practicing for <6 months ( P < 0.05). Oxygen saturation and peak expiratory flow rate were significantly higher in the >6-month group ( P < 0.001). Waist–hip ratio did not differ significantly between the groups. Conclusion: Longer duration of yoga practice was associated with more beneficial anthropometric, cardiovascular, and respiratory parameters among healthy adults. Future longitudinal studies using standardized yoga protocols are warranted to further clarify the relationship between yoga practice duration and physiological and cardiopulmonary outcomes.

title: Peran Psikologi Komunikasi dalam Mendukung Kepercayaan Diri Anak melalui Kegiatan Lomba Islam Anak Ceria di Desa Gaden
abstractText: This community service study examines the role of communication psychology in fostering children's self-confidence through the “Lomba Islami Anak Ceria” (Cheerful Islamic Children's Competition) held at At-Taqwa Mosque, Gaden Village, Trucuk District, Klaten Regency. The program was initiated following observations that many early childhood and elementary school children attending local Quranic learning centers lacked self-confidence, felt shy, and hesitated to perform publicly. The study employed a participatory approach integrating communication psychology principles, supported by evaluation through direct observation and qualitative reflection. The program consisted of three stages: preparation through TPA mentoring, implementation of competitions, and evaluation. Activities included adhan recitation, Islamic quizzes, calligraphy coloring, short surah recitation, and interactive quizzes. Approximately 100 children from TPAs across Gaden Village participated, supported by 21 student volunteers. The results showed that friendly, empathetic, and supportive communication strategies, combined with equal appreciation for all participants, created a safe and comfortable social environment. Children demonstrated greater enthusiasm, more active participation, and increased courage in interacting and expressing themselves publicly. These findings highlight the importance of positive communication in supporting children's psychological development. This study concludes that a supportive environment grounded in communication psychology can effectively foster self-confidence in early childhood, particularly through engaging, inclusive, and enjoyable Islamic educational activities.

abstractText: This study aims to analyze the influence ofself-concept, social influence, lifestyle, and price perception on Generation Z customers' purchase intention for skincare products at Duta Kosmetik Store in Bireuen Regency. This associative quantitative study involved 95 respondents selected through purposive sampling criteria: Generation Z born between 1997–2012, residing in Bireuen Regency, and having purchased skincare products at Duta Kosmetik Store at least once. Primary data were collected using a structured Likert scale (1 –5) questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression via SPSS version 26. Partial t-test results demonstrate that self-concept positively and significantly influences purchase intention (tcount = 2.403 > ttable = 1 .661 ; sig = 0.018). Social influence also has a positive and significant effect (tcount = 3.076 > ttable = 1 .661 ; sig = 0.003). Lifestyle exerts a positive and significant impact (tcount = 2.360 > ttable = 1 .661 ; sig = 0.020), and price perception demonstrates the most dominant positive and significant impact (tcount = 3.685 > ttable = 1 .661 ; sig = 0.000). Simultaneously, all four independent variables significantly affect purchase intention with Fcount = 10.140 > Ftable = 2.47 (sig = 0.000). The correlation coefficient (R = 0.557) indicates a moderately strong relationship, and the Adjusted R2 = 0.280 reveals that 28.0% ofpurchase intention variance is explained by these four predictors.

Claims-based frailty, dual eligibility, and potential unmet home-health needs in older breast cancer survivors
abstractText: Abstract Background Older breast cancer survivors often need home-based functional support, yet whether Medicare’s restricted home health (HH) benefit leaves frailty-related need unmet at the population level is not quantified because measurement is lacking. Methods Using linked Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare-OASIS data, we studied 347 953 survivor-years during 2017-2020 from 134 410 women with invasive breast cancer 2-10 years post-diagnosis. We derived a claims-based predicted deficit-accumulation frailty index (DAFI), calibrated by penalized elastic-net to the observed OASIS Start-of-Care DAFI, the HH-need benchmark. Outcomes were any Medicare HH use and potential unmet need, defined as no HH use among high-need survivor-years (predicted DAFI ≥ 0.25). Logistic models estimated the marginal effects of DAFI on any Medicare HH use by frailty and dual eligibility, and disparities in potential unmet need. Results The claims-based DAFI was closely calibrated to observed OASIS DAFI (area under the curve = 0.715; slope = 1.111). Any HH use rose with frailty (+1.10 percentage points [pp] per +0.01 DAFI; 95% CI = 1.05 to 1.15), most steeply among never-dual survivors (+1.21 pp; 95% CI = 1.16 to 1.26) and less steeply among always-dual survivors (+0.41 pp; 95% CI = 0.30 to 0.53). Among high-need survivor years, 59.6% had no Medicare HH use. Long-term survivors had similar DAFI to 2-5-year survivors (0.216 vs 0.215) and lower HH use, but potential unmet need did not differ. Conclusions A claims-based frailty proxy reveals potential frailty-related needs that Medicare HH does not reach. Expanding Medicare HH to better cover personal care and other home- and community-based services may help address frailty-related needs.

Impact of Triple Assessment on Surgical Decision-making in Thyroid Nodule Management
abstractText: Abstract Introduction: Accurate preoperative assessment of thyroid nodules is crucial for distinguishing malignant from benign lesions and making optimal decisions. Triple assessment using clinical examination, ultrasonography (USG), and fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) has been increasingly used to improve diagnostic accuracy. Aim: The aim of the study was to evaluate the efficacy of triple assessment in the detection and treatment of thyroid nodules by correlating ultrasonographic findings, clinical evaluation, and FNAC results with histopathological diagnosis. Methods: This study was a prospective observational study of 56 patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgical management. Data were collected prospectively using structured case record forms. Baseline information, physical examination findings, USG features, FNAC records, operative details, and histopathological reports were documented. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Frequency and percentage were used to present categorical variables. The diagnostic accuracy of clinical examination, USG, FNAC, and triple assessment was evaluated by estimating specificity, sensitivity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value, and diagnostic accuracy. Results: A higher proportion of participants were female (85.7%) and were in the 41–60 years old age group. Histopathology confirmed benign lesions in 57.14% and malignant lesions in 42.86% of cases. Triple assessment achieved the most effective diagnostic accuracy, showing a sensitivity of 100%, a specificity of 87.50%, with a NPV of 100% and an overall diagnostic accuracy of 97.86%. Conclusion: Triple assessment is a dependable and useful modality for assessing thyroid nodules. Combined use of clinical examination, USG, and FNAC reduces false-negative results and supports appropriate clinical decision-making.

Interventions targeting cardiometabolic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in pregnancy in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs); a systematic review with focus on complex interventions
abstractText: Abstract Background Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as diabetes, hypertension, and obesity are increasingly recognised important causes of adverse pregnancy outcomes in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite this growing burden, few large-scale programmes exist to tackle NCDs in pregnancy in these settings. Identification of complex interventions that may be transferable to similar contexts is an important component of future intervention development. Methods We conducted a systematic review to characterise interventions addressing NCDs in pregnancy across LMICs. We included experimental, quasi-experimental, and pre-experimental studies targeting diabetes, hypertension, obesity and chronic kidney disease, or related gestational syndromes among pregnant women or those in the pre-conception or postpartum periods. Searches were conducted in Scopus, MEDLINE, CINAHL, PubMed and Cochrane CENTRAL from 1 January 1990 to 14 June 2024. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted using COVIDENCE software. Intervention complexity was assessed using the Cochrane iCAT_SR tool. Complex interventions underwent risk of bias assessment, and all studies underwent credibility checks using open-source databases. Review conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Results Of 3,477 records screened, 135 studies were included. Most were small, single site trials conducted in tertiary care facilities. Leading contributors were Iran (27%), China (16%) and India (13%), whilst only ten studies (7%) originated from sub-Saharan Africa. Less than one quarter (31/135, 23%) targeted women with underlying NCDs; most focussed on gestational syndromes such as gestational diabetes or pre-eclampsia. Interventions primarily targeted individual participants rather than wider health systems, commonly using educational or pharmacological approaches. Approximately one quarter (37/135, 27%) of studies reported formal intervention design processes or stakeholder involvement. Seventeen studies were classified as complex interventions (iCAT_SR ≥ 12/18), of which 59% (10/17) were judged at high risk of bias. Compared with simple interventions, complex interventions more frequently reported implementation outcomes (41% vs 8%), stakeholder involvement (65% vs 14%), and intervention design processes (82% vs 19%). Conclusions We demonstrate a marked shortage of complex, system-level interventions addressing NCDs in pregnancy across LMICs. Future intervention design should prioritise co-designed, multi-level interventions with embedded implementation outcomes, particularly in under-represented regions such as sub-Saharan Africa. This review provides a practical resource for researchers and policy makers seeking adaptable and scalable interventions for use in comparable settings. Trial registration PROSPERO CRD42025643691

title: Revisión sistemática sobre el Invierte.pe y la inversión pública en el Perú
abstractText: Este artículo de revisión aborda la evolución del Sistema Nacional de Programación Multianual y Gestión de Inversiones – Invierte.pe, resaltando su papel en la modernización de la gestión de la inversión pública en el Perú. Su objetivo principal es evaluar cómo este sistema ha mejorado la eficiencia, transparencia y sostenibilidad en el uso de los recursos públicos, orientando las inversiones hacia el cierre de brechas sociales y territoriales. La metodología empleada fue una revisión sistemática cualitativa, basada en el análisis de artículos académicos publicados entre 2018 y 2025 en bases de datos como Scielo, Redalyc y Dialnet. El estudio se centra en la evolución del sistema desde la transición del antiguo SNIP hacia Invierte.pe, destacando los avances en la programación multianual, formulación, ejecución y evaluación ex post de proyectos. Asimismo, resalta la incorporación de herramientas digitales como el Banco de Inversiones y los sistemas de seguimiento físico-financiero, que fortalecen la rendición de cuentas y la planificación estratégica. Se concluye que el Invierte.pe constituye una herramienta clave para la eficiencia del gasto público y el desarrollo sostenible, aunque aún enfrenta retos en la capacitación técnica y la gestión territorial.

Vitamin A and Zinc Profile of Plasmodium falciparum Malaria in Selected Communities in Delta Central Senatorial District, Delta State, Nigeria
abstractText: Malaria remains a major public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa, where micronutrient deficiencies may complicate infection. This study assessed malaria parasitemia intensity and serum vitamin A and zinc concentrations in Delta Central Senatorial District, Delta State, Nigeria. Thick blood film microscopy was used to examine 566 participants for malaria parasitemia. Serum vitamin A and zinc concentrations were measured in a subset of 50 parasitemic volunteers using the Carr–Price colorimetric method and flame atomic absorption spectrophotometry, respectively. Analysis of variance was used to compare micronutrient concentrations between parasitemic participants and uninfected controls. Moderate parasitemia (1,000–9,999 parasites/µL) predominated (75.8%), followed by mild parasitemia (24.2%). No parasite densities of ≥10,000 parasites/µL were observed. Serum vitamin A and zinc concentrations were numerically higher in parasitemic participants than in uninfected controls, but neither difference was statistically significant (p > .05). The findings document a predominance of moderate parasitemia without statistically significant differences in the measured micronutrient concentrations between infected participants and controls. This study provides local evidence to inform malaria control strategies that consider both infection and nutritional status in endemic populations.

title: Analysis of the complex relationship between parental response and purpose in Chinese children’s life: a study using network analysis
abstractText: Abstract Background Parental responses to children’s negative emotions (PRCNE) play a crucial role in child development, yet their relationship with children’s purpose in life (CPL) remains underexplored. Given that Chinese parents attach great importance to gender-differentiated child-rearing, it is imperative to investigate gender-based variations in children’s perceptions of PRCNE and their associations with the construction of meaning in CPL. Purpose This study aimed to investigate: (1) the interconnections among perceived dimensions of PRCNE; (2) the pattern of associations linking perceived PRCNE dimensions to children’s CPL, thereby extending the literature on parental behaviors and child development; and (3) the boundary role of gender by examining gender differences in both the perceived PRCNE patterns and their associations with CPL. Methods Data were collected from a sample of 573 Chinese students between March and June 2024, and network analysis was conducted. Given the study’s focus on pairwise variable associations, strength centrality and bridge strength were jointly examined to identify key nodes and meaningful connections within the networks. Results Network comparisons within the PRCNE network revealed that problem-focused response was the most central node among boys (centrality = 1.142), whereas emotion-focused response was the most central node among girls (centrality = 1.085). In the combined PRCNE–CPL network, minimization response emerged as the strongest bridge node and was positively associated with beyond-self orientation (weight = 0.112). While global network structures were invariant across gender, localized differences in specific edge weights suggested that girls’ networks exhibited tighter clustering of negative responses. Furthermore, the assocaition between problem-focused response and meaningfulness was significantly stronger for boys than for girls ( p = 0.034), while the edge between emotion-focused response and goal-directedness appeared only for girls ( p = 0.055). Conclusion These findings indicate that children’s perceptions of PRCNE reflect a mixed pattern: overall, boys perceived a greater emphasis on problem-solving responses, while girls perceived a greater emphasis on emotional support. Minimization response is positively associated with goal directedness, suggesting it may co-occur with aspects of children’s purpose development. Gender-stratified analyses further revealed that the difference of purpose built between problem-focused response among boys and emotion-focused response girls. These results underscore the importance of perceived PRCNE for children’s development and broaden the research significance of family education.

title: Comparative Profiling of Arterial Stiffness and Radiocephalic Arteriovenous Fistula Morphology in Diabetic Versus Non-Diabetic Patients on Maintenance Hemodialysis
abstractText: Background: Diabetes mellitus accelerates cardiovascular deterioration in chronic kidney disease, but it is unclear whether it adds stiffness to the central arteries or affects the peripheral arteriovenous fistula (AVF) of hemodialysis patients. Objective: To compare central and peripheral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV, faPWV), renal resistive index (RI), and radiocephalic AVF diameter and volume flow between diabetic and non-diabetic hemodialysis patients. Methods: This analytical cross-sectional study included 120 prevalent hemodialysis patients (22 diabetic, 98 non-diabetic) at Dr. M. Djamil General Hospital in 2025. One blinded sonographer measured the vascular parameters by Doppler ultrasonography. Groups were compared with t-tests and chi-square tests, with 95% confidence intervals and Cohen's d. Results: Diabetic patients were older (56.4 ± 8.1 vs. 50.6 ± 9.4 years; p = 0.004) and had lower diastolic blood pressure (73.27 ± 9.84 vs. 79.72 ± 10.15 mmHg; p = 0.008). cfPWV (2.89 ± 0.57 vs. 2.90 ± 0.61 m/s; p = 0.941), faPWV (3.34 ± 0.73 vs. 3.15 ± 0.69 m/s; p = 0.236), and mean RI (0.825 ± 0.029 vs. 0.818 ± 0.033; p = 0.341) did not differ. AVF diameter was smaller in diabetic patients (1.74 ± 0.63 vs. 2.36 ± 0.74 mm; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = −0.86), whereas flow did not differ significantly (3489 ± 1018 vs. 3063 ± 945 mL/min; p = 0.072). Conclusion: Diabetes was associated with a smaller AVF diameter but not with higher central or peripheral stiffness or renal RI. Given the cross-sectional, unadjusted design, adjusted longitudinal studies are needed.

abstractText: The quality of BPJS administrative services affects patient satisfaction with healtcare services. title: Longitudinal association between body weight change and brachial–ankle pulse wave velocity in patients with treated hypertension or diabetes mellitus: A post hoc analysis of the FMD-J study B
abstractText: Abstract We investigated cross-sectional associations between body mass index (BMI) and brachial–ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and longitudinal associations between body weight change and baPWV over 3 years in 874 patients with treated hypertension or diabetes mellitus without coronary artery disease (475 men; mean age, 61.9 ± 9.5 years). baPWV was measured at baseline, 1.5 years, and 3 years. At baseline, BMI was inversely correlated with baPWV ( r = −0.14, P < 0.001), and multivariate analysis confirmed this association (β = −12.5, P < 0.001). In generalized linear mixed-effects models adjusted for concurrent systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and other covariates, neither continuous percentage change in body weight (β = −1.2, P = 0.08) nor categorical body weight change (≥5% increase: β = −10.6, P = 0.45; ≥5% decrease: β = 18.0, P = 0.15) was associated with longitudinal changes in baPWV, with no interaction across baseline BMI categories. The modest body weight changes observed in this cohort were not significantly associated with longitudinal changes in baPWV.

title: Recent achievements of the National Center Biobank Network (NCBN) bioresources through Japanese fiscal year 2025
abstractText: The National Center Biobank Network (NCBN) is constituted by a network of biobanks from five National Centers and the Japan Institute for Health Security (JIHS). The NCBN primarily collects samples from patients with various diseases, amassing a total of more than 250,000 participants and 800,000 human biospecimens as of the end of March 2026. The primary sample types are blood and DNA, with spinal fluid and frozen tissue samples also collected depending on the characteristics of the disease. These samples are accompanied by highly specialized and traceable clinical information supported by advanced medical care and expertise. Moreover, some samples are accompanied by whole-genome sequencing data. Consequently, these resources provide a unique platform for translational research, biomarker discovery, and genomic medicine in Japan. In the present review, we provide a detailed account of the recent achievements of NCBN biobanks and their biospecimens and genomic data.

title: Description of a new species and a new record of Sandperch of genus Parapercis (Perciformes: Pinguipedidae) from Indian waters
abstractText: A new species of Sandperch, Parapercis bengalensis sp. nov., is described based on four specimens (84.58–89.18 mm SL) collected from commercial trawl catch landings operated at depths of 30–80 m in the Bay of Bengal, India. Parapercis bengalensis sp. nov. is distinguishable from its congeners by presence of three large and five small black rounded blotch below lateral line, extending from behind the pectoral fin base to caudal end; presence of palatine teeth on upper jaw; presence of small orange colour dots on the ventral side of the body below lateral line, extending from the pectoral-fin base to the caudal base; upper portion of lateral line with numerous small black dot extending from behind the eye to the caudal base; caudal base with two black spots, chin and snout with an orange colour line; the entire dorsal fin is translucent with numerous small black spots. The species appears to be widely distributed in the Bay of Bengal, as the specimens were collected from off Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Digha, and Chennai along the east coast of India. Furthermore, Parapercis caudopellucida Johnson & Motomura, 2017 is recorded for the first time from Indian waters based on a single specimen collected from commercial trawl bycatch operated at depths of 30–80 m off Kollam, Kerala, in the Arabian Sea.

abstractText: Predicting stock fluctuations is extremely important for risk management and asset allocation. Traditional models like Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH) cannot handle the complex and ever-changing stock market data, so machine learning prediction methods have been widely adopted. This paper conducts a review study by collecting relevant literature. The research steps are as follows: first, screen the relevant literature on stock volatility prediction; then, divide the models in the literature into two categories: traditional machine learning and deep learning; next, compare the application scenarios, actual effects, and shortcomings of each type of model, and summarize the common methods used in existing research for data processing and feature creation. After organizing the data, it was found that this industry has three main practical problems: the predicted results given by the model are unclear in terms of their causes, the predictions are inaccurate in different market environments, and it is difficult to develop high-quality analytical indicators. To address these issues, several research directions can be proposed: developing a logically understandable combined model that can adapt to different markets and combine data from various sources for use. This review can provide a reference for those who will conduct related research in the future.

abstractText: Percina crypta Freeman, Freeman & Burkhead, the Halloween Darter, was described in 2008 as a new species endemic to the Chattahoochee and Flint River systems in the Apalachicola Basin, Georgia and Alabama, USA. The description illustrated phenotypic differences between Percina crypta and sympatric Percina nigrofasciata (Agassiz) sensu lato (s.l.) (the Blackbanded Darter) but lacked genetic data. Because of certain morphological similarities with syntopic Percina nigrofasciata s.l. and anecdotal evidence suggesting low genetic differentiation between the two forms, recent authors have noted the need for additional investigations to assess the taxonomic validity of Percina crypta. To examine whether P. crypta represents a valid species separate from P. nigrofasciata s.l., we used 3RAD reduced-representation genomic data and expanded phenotypic comparisons between P. crypta and P. nigrofasciata s.l. from the Apalachicola basin and three adjacent river basins. Genome-wide sequence data show that P. crypta is reciprocally monophyletic with respect to P. nigrofasciata s.l. in every basin examined. Meristic and morphometric data also resolve P. crypta and P. nigrofasciata s.l. as distinct clusters in principal component analyses, and pigmentation patterns provide diagnostic characters that allow easy identification of P. crypta in the field. Additionally, we provide preliminary genomic, meristic, and morphological data that suggest populations of the Percina nigrofasciata complex in the Apalachicola, Altamaha, and Savannah basins, which have recently been collectively referred to under the epithet “westfalli” (Fowler), comprise at least two distinct species. We treat Apalachicola populations as an undescribed form, Percina sp. cf. nigrofasciata, that occurs sympatrically with P. crypta. Our conclusion that P. crypta is a valid species supports conservation status for the species in Georgia and Alabama. Ongoing work by the present authors aims to elucidate patterns of speciation in this group and to clarify taxonomy of the eastern populations of the Percina nigrofasciata complex.

Prevalence, determinants and outcomes of intravenous to oral switch of antibiotic therapy in hospitalized adults with bloodstream infection: secondary analysis of a multicenter cohort
abstractText: Abstract Background Intravenous to oral switch (IVOS) is considered safe in selected patients with bloodstream infection and provides operational advantages. Still, it is underused in many clinical settings. We evaluated IVOS patterns, associated factors and clinical outcomes in patients with bloodstream infection. Methods Secondary data from two prospective, multicenter cohort studies recruiting patients with bloodstream infection were analyzed. IVOS was assessed on day 3 and 7 after positive blood culture. Eligibility for IVOS was based on infectious focus, clinical safe switch criteria and antimicrobial susceptibility. Risk factors for non-IVOS were studied using multivariable logistic regression. Results Among 3824 patients, 2770 were included in secondary analysis, and 742 (19.4%) were eligible and evaluable for IVOS. By day 7, 240 patients (32.3%) underwent IVOS. Switch occurred on the day of discharge in 107 patients (44.6%), and one day before in 46 (19.2%). Most commonly used oral agents were ciprofloxacin (75 patients, 31.3%), sultamicillin (56, 23.3%), and cefuroxime axetil (27, 11.3%). Upon multivariable analysis, diabetes (OR=0.57 (0.38-0.88), p=0.010), chronic kidney disease (0.64 (0.41-0.99), p=0.048), Pitt bacteremia score ≥ 2 on day 3 (0.43 (0.19-0.97), p=0.042) and septic shock before day 7 (0.31 (0.11-0.87), p=0.027) were barriers to IVOS, while urogenital focus (2.22 (1.50-3.28), p<0.001) and two study centers were positively associated with IVOS. IVOS was associated with shorter length of stay (7 vs. 12 days, p<0.001) and lower 28-day mortality. Conclusions In clinically stable patients with bloodstream infection, IVOS was infrequently implemented. Barriers to IVOS should be addressed as part of antimicrobial stewardship programs.

title: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human–Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication
abstractText: Abstract Silent speech decoding (lip reading) represents an innovative hands-free communication method for individuals with laryngeal and lingual impairments, addressing critical daily communication challenges. Herein, a novel silent speech decoding system is proposed, which employs a self-powered, low-cost, and conformable triboelectric-based E‑skin patch and a well-trained multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) model. We systematically characterize the structural principles and electrical performance of the E-skin patch. A comparative analysis of labial kinematics during vocalized and silent speech is also conducted, which demonstrates strong consistency in time–frequency domain characteristics. The utilized CNN model is trained across 15 lexical categories (200 samples per category), achieving a high accuracy of 98.75% and demonstrating excellent recognition performance. Furthermore, by integrating human–machine interaction (HMI) and virtual reality (VR) technologies, we develop three representative applications, including a real-time lip language visualization system, an orofacial-controlled “Feeding Frenzy” interactive game, and a VR communication platform with avatar dialogue. This technology enables barrier-free communication for voiceless populations, demonstrating significant potential in HMI, augmentative communication systems, virtual reality integration, and biomedical rehabilitation.

title: Intrapleural TPA vs Normal Saline in Pediatric Empyema: A Comparative Study
abstractText: OBJECTIVE To determine whether intrapleural tissue plasminogen activator (TPA) reduces hospital length of stay (LOS) vs intrapleural normal saline in children with complicated parapneumonic effusion or empyema. METHODS A retrospective cohort study at a tertiary pediatric referral hospital in Iran, comparing children aged 1 month to 18 years treated during TPA unavailability (2012–2015; intrapleural saline, 40 mL, 1-hour dwell, daily ×3 days) with those treated after TPA became available (2015–2018; TPA 4 mg in 40 mL saline, same protocol). The primary outcome was hospital LOS, and the secondary outcomes were intensive care unit (ICU) stay, fever duration, chest-tube duration, and ICU admission. Multivariable linear regression was adjusted for baseline imbalances between cohorts. RESULTS Of 85 patients, 61 received TPA and 24 saline. The cohorts were comparable at baseline, except for higher pleural fluid adenosine deaminase and shorter time to first instillation in the saline group (medium and very large effects). The mean hospital LOS was 20.28 ± 5.53 days (TPA) vs 19.17 ± 3.60 days (saline). The unadjusted difference was 1.11 days (95% CI, −1.14 to 3.36; P = .366). The adjusted mean difference was 0.36 days (95% CI, −2.91 to 3.63; P = .826). Secondary outcomes showed similarly small differences, with CI ranges compatible with no clinically important effect. CONCLUSIONS Intrapleural TPA showed no detectable benefit over saline in this retrospective comparison. The wide CI ranges indicate insufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis and not equivalence. Our findings raise, but do not confirm, the hypothesis that mechanical lavage contributes to clinical improvement. Residual confounding and selection bias cannot be excluded. Adequately powered, prospective randomized trials are needed to establish the incremental value of fibrinolysis in children.

abstractText: The article examines subjective representations of health among preschool education teachers as a subject of psychological analysis and a basis for organizing professional support. The aim of the study is to reveal the content of these representations and substantiate an approach to their investigation, taking into account the conditions of pedagogical work. The study employs a theoretical and analytical review of research on self-rated health, psychological well- being, and teacher support. The assessment of one’s own health status, health satisfaction, and social comparison are distinguished. An analytical framework is proposed that links these components to the professional context and everyday decisions regarding recovery. The article highlights the limitations of interpreting self-reports and transferring international research findings to different educational environments. Directions for further empirical research and practical recommendations for preschool institutions are formulated. The study is theoretical in nature and does not contain results from an original empirical assessment.

title: Concussion Safety Beliefs and Participation Decisions Among US Adults With a History of Concussion
abstractText: Introduction Concussion safety education must address specific participation decisions as well as general beliefs. Method An anonymous, opt-in online survey of 100 US adults with self-reported concussion history was analyzed descriptively. Results Ninety-one percent endorsed avoiding same-day return after suspected concussion, and 81% would not allow a child to continue immediately after a “mild” concussion. Among the 91 endorsing no same-day return, 9 would allow immediate continuation, 7 selected sport-dependent participation, and 2 were unsure. Medical clearance was supported by 88% on an agreement item, whereas 77% selected clearance after every concussion on a separate question. Conclusions Responses varied across differently worded safety questions; they do not establish actual behavior or national prevalence. Practical Applications Education could distinguish immediate removal from later graduated return and explicitly address injuries described as mild. These descriptive findings support testing such messages, rather than demonstrating their effectiveness.

Systematic identification of characteristic chemical constituents in Cistanches Herba from saline-alkali land based on hierarchical filtering of mass spectrometry data and spatial metabolomics technology
abstractText: Abstract Background The traditional habitat of the Chinese medicinal plant Cistanches Herba (CH) is the deserts of northwestern China. Recently, CH cultivation has been introduced to saline-alkali land (SAL) in the Yellow River delta region. However, the effects of this SAL environment on the accumulation of secondary metabolites in CH remain unclear. Objective This research aims to systematically characterize the chemical profiles of CH grown in SAL and to identify key chemical markers associated with the SAL environment. Methods CH samples were collected from both SAL and traditional sandy land (SL). Untargeted metabolomics was performed using ultra performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS) to characterize the global metabolic profiles of CH from two habitats. Chemical markers associated with SAL environments were screened via weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), targeted quantification by ultra performance liquid chromatography-triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (UPLC-TQ-MS), and compound loading contributions of principal component analysis (PCA). Subsequently, desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging (DESI-MSI) was employed to visualize the in situ spatial distribution of partial screened constituents in mouse organs. Results Untargeted UPLC-QTOF-MS metabolomics identified 74 chemical constituents from CH samples, including 40 phenylethanoid glycosides, 13 iridoid glycosides, 9 lignans, and other minor constituents. Orthogonal projections to latent structures-discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) clearly separated the SAL and SL sample groups, with 30 constituents showing prominent contributions to the discrimination. WGCNA revealed 23 metabolites correlated with SAL. By integrating these two screening methods, 12 constituents were preliminarily selected as candidate markers associated with SAL. Subsequently, combining PCA loading coefficients (with the PCA model validated by Kaiser–Meyer–Olkin and Bartlett’s sphericity tests) and targeted UPLC-TQ-MS quantification, 4 constituents-verbascoside, echinacoside, isoacteoside, and pinoresinol- were ultimately identified as characteristic chemical markers, all exhibiting significantly higher levels in SAL samples. DESI-MSI results further demonstrated that echinacoside predominantly accumulated in brain tissue, whereas verbascoside or isoacteoside displayed the strongest ion signal in the lung. Conclusion This study developed an integrated strategy that combines hierarchical filtering of mass spectrometry data to successfully identify 4 characteristic chemical markers of CH associated with SAL. This strategy provides a scientific basis for future quality control and resource development.
